docs.text: Setting What it does NONE The target is scanned only when SecurityBoat runs a scan on demand. It counts as unmonitored. DAILY / WEEKLY / MONTHLY The target is rescanned automatically every day, week, or month once it is Active. Freshness SLA How long a scan result stays "fresh". By default it is a little longer than the rescan interval; set an override to tighten or relax it. When results go stale the target is flagged on the Dashboard's Coverage SLA panel.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No Request Scan button, or Access denied Only Client Admin can request targets. My target is still Pending review SecurityBoat has not approved it yet. Add detail in the reviewer note, or ask your CSM. My target was Rejected Hover over the badge to read the reason, then submit a corrected request. I can't change the target value It is fixed once the target is approved. Request a new target instead. Cloud validation keeps failing Re-check the credentials and permissions, and confirm they have not expired. "ASM Module Not Enabled" ASM is not enabled for your organisation. Contact your CSM.

← Previous: Dashboard | Next: Scans →

docs.title: Asset Detail
docs.text: The Asset Details page provides a centralized, read-only view of a single asset's configuration, credentials, attachments, and testing history.

docs.title: 1. Header Actions
docs.text:
For users with Client Admin or Client TPM privileges, the header displays several management tools:

Action Control Behaviour Typical Use Case Edit Opens the asset editing interface. Modify the description, change the owner, alter target types, or update the scope. Archive Triggers an archive confirmation dialog. Transitions the asset state to Archived. Remove retired or decommissioned assets from default view lists without destroying their history. Restore Appears in place of "Archive" for archived assets. Returns state to Active. Re-enable an asset that has been put back into testing rotation. Clone Opens a dialog requesting a new name. Duplicates metadata and scope contract. Quickly spin up a similar environment (e.g., creating a -staging counterpart to a -prod asset). Back Returns you directly to the main Assets list page. Navigation shortcut.

docs.title: Why Archiving is Preferred Over Deletion
docs.text:
Tri-Netra does not support hard-deleting assets. This is a deliberate design choice:

  • Audit Trails: Security reports, historical pentests, and active findings are linked to the asset record. Deleting an asset would orphan these records and break compliance audit trails.
  • Safety Valve: Archiving hides the asset from active dropdowns and dashboards but preserves its entire history.
  • Active Engagement Lock: The platform actively blocks archiving if the asset is currently referenced in a live, active pentest engagement. You must complete or cancel the engagement before you can archive the asset.

docs.title: 2. Tabbed Submodules In-Depth
docs.text: The body of the details page is split into five tabs:

docs.title: a. Overview Tab
docs.text:
Provides a high-level summary of the asset's metadata and description.

  • Description: Displays the formatted rich-text description. If diagrams or images were pasted into the description editor, they render inline here.
  • Metadata Cards:
  • Types: Lists the selected categories (Web App, API, Mobile, etc.).
  • Criticality: Displays the color-coded criticality pill (Critical → Informational).
  • State: Displays the active state badge.
  • Owner: Identifies the assigned technical or business owner.
  • Created: Shows the creation date and the name of the user who registered it.
  • Updated: Shows the timestamp of the last modification.

docs.title: b. Scope Tab
docs.text:
Displays the type-specific targets set in the scope contract:

  • Web Applications / APIs: Shows lists of verified URLs or base endpoints. If documentation (like Postman collections, OpenAPI/Swagger specifications, or architecture diagrams) is attached, clicking the link downloads the file.
  • Mobile Apps: Lists Store links, uploaded APK/IPA binaries, and special instructions.
  • Network & Infrastructure: Shows a paginated list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges (10 rows per page) alongside VPN configuration notes.

docs.title: c. Credentials Tab
docs.text:
Manages test credentials for the asset. Client Viewers can see that credentials exist but cannot view secrets.

  • Auditable Reveals: Clicking the reveal icon on a password or API key decrypts it on the fly. To prevent credential abuse, every reveal is tracked. The system records the name of the user, the timestamp, and the credential label, and retains this audit trail for 7 years.
  • In-Place Additions: Client Admins and TPMs can click Add credential to supply new login sets directly from this tab.
  • Deletion: Obsolete credential sets can be removed using the trash icon (requires confirmation).

docs.title: d. Attachments Tab
docs.text:
Hosts files uploaded via the Scope Details section (architecture diagrams, Postman collections, OpenAPI specs, APK/IPA binaries, etc.).

How files arrive here: Files are not uploaded directly on this tab. When you upload a document inside a Scope detail input (e.g., an architecture diagram for a Web Application or an OpenAPI spec for an API), it is automatically surfaced in the Attachments tab once the virus scan completes.

  • Virus Scanning Lifecycle: Every file uploaded undergoes an automated security scan:
  • Scanning...: The file is undergoing verification. Downloads are disabled.
  • Clean: The scan passed. The file is accessible to authorized testers and download icons are enabled.
  • Infected - Quarantined: The file failed the scan. The system locks down the file, blocks downloads, and flags it as quarantined.
  • Unlinking: Users can remove files by clicking the trash icon next to the attachment.

docs.title: e. Usage Tab
docs.text:
Provides a rollup of the asset's security testing history within your organization:

  • Displays the total count of pentest engagements referencing the asset.
  • Lists recent engagements showing their title, project ID, state (e.g., Draft, In Progress, Completed), and creation date.
  • Provides a quick link (View →) to jump directly to the specific PTaaS engagement.

← Previous: Create Asset | Next: Edit Asset

docs.title: Create Asset
docs.text: Only users with Client Admin or Client TPM roles can create new assets. For read-only users, the buttons to add or import assets are hidden.

docs.title: 1. Manual Asset Creation — Step-by-Step
docs.text:
Click New asset on the Assets list page to launch the creation form. The form is structured into numbered sections to help you build the asset profile systematically.

A sticky footer at the bottom tracks your progress, displaying a count of completed required fields (e.g., N / total required fields ready). The Create asset button is enabled only when all required inputs are valid.

Scope Isolation: The form is automatically scoped to your organisation; you cannot accidentally assign assets to a different business entity.

docs.title: Section 1 — Basic Information
docs.text:
Configure the identifier and business value of the asset.

Field Type Required Validation / Limits Purpose Asset name Text ✅ ≤ 255 characters; must be unique within your organization (case-insensitive). The primary label used throughout the platform (e.g., in reports and engagement scopes). Criticality Single-select dropdown ✅ One of 5 levels. Defaults to Medium. The business risk level. Used to prioritize finding triage. Description Rich Text Editor — No strict limit. Supports markdown formatting and image pasting. Business context for testers (what it does, user types, known restrictions).

docs.title: Choosing Criticality Levels
docs.text:
Set asset criticality realistically. Over-inflating all assets to "Critical" dilutes the value of prioritisation for your security team.

Level Guidelines for Selection Impact on Testing Critical Core business-critical application. Compromise causes severe business disruption. Findings trigger immediate alert escalation; fixes block releases. High Customer-facing apps handling sensitive data (PII, financials) or core APIs. Vulnerabilities prioritized for rapid turnaround. Medium Internal tools, corporate services, or staging environments (default). Standard patch cycle and notification urgency. Low Read-only sites, marketing pages, or isolated utilities. Bounded risk; resolved within standard SLA windows. Informational Dev environments or sandboxes containing no production data. Awareness-only tracking; findings do not affect posture scoring.

docs.title: Section 2 — Asset Type Picker
docs.text:
Select up to 3 types that represent the asset. Picking a type dynamically unlocks its corresponding Scope Details input fields in Section 3.

Why support multiple types? Real-world products often span multiple layers. For example, a single product might consist of a Web Application interface, a backing API, and a Mobile App. Grouping them under a single asset keeps the security posture and findings cohesive rather than fragmenting them across separate records.

docs.title: Section 3 — Scope Details (The Scope Contract)
docs.text:
This section acts as a "contract" between you and the security Researchers. Researchers will only test targets explicitly listed here. Any unlisted infrastructure or endpoints are considered out-of-scope.

Depending on the types selected in Section 2, provide the following details:

  • Web Application: Specify one or more URLs (e.g., https://app.example.com). You can add URLs individually or use Import CSV/TXT to batch-paste a list. You can also upload an architecture diagram or auth-flow document (up to 50 MB per file).
  • API & Web Services: Provide base URLs (e.g., https://api.example.com/v1). You can upload a Postman collection (JSON) or OpenAPI/Swagger spec (JSON/YAML) to let testers immediately map out the endpoints.
  • Mobile (Android/iOS): Provide at least one of the following: a Store URL, an uploaded binary (.apk or .ipa), or testing instructions.
  • Network & Infrastructure: Populate a targets table with IPs or CIDR ranges (up to 5,000 targets). You can import targets via a simple CSV format. Add VPN notes and upload network diagrams as needed.
  • Cloud, Thick Client, IoT, Hardware, Telecom, Physical, Other: Enter descriptive notes (up to 2,000 characters) and upload one supporting document (up to 50 MB).

Behind the Scenes: The details are compiled into a structured JSON scope contract (maximum 2 MB). Files are staged locally in your browser and uploaded to the platform's secure storage when you submit the form.

docs.title: Section 4 — Credentials (Optional)
docs.text:
Provide test account details to allow authenticated security testing.

Field Type Required Notes Label Text ✅ A descriptive identifier (e.g., Standard User, Manager Role). Username Text — Account login or email. Secret Password ✅ The password, token, or key. Notes Text — Special instructions (e.g., "MFA has been bypassed for this source IP").

Security & Encryption: To protect sensitive accounts, secrets are encrypted at rest at the database layer immediately upon save. Because they are securely hashed and stored, they cannot be read back from the form or the edit page. Credential management (revealing, adding, or deleting) is handled entirely via the Credentials tab on the Asset Details page.

docs.title: Submitting the Form
docs.text: Click Create asset. If a file upload fails during submission, the asset record is still saved, and a warning informs you which file upload failed so you can retry it on the asset's edit page.

docs.title: 2. Bulk Creation via CSV Import
docs.text: When onboarding a large inventory of assets, use the bulk import feature.

docs.title: CSV File Schema
docs.text:
To avoid parsing errors, download the layout structure using the Download template button.

Column Header Required Valid Formats / Values Purpose name ✅ Text (≤ 255 chars); unique within organization The asset name. type ✅ Web Application, API & Web Services, Mobile (Android), Mobile (iOS), Network & Infrastructure, etc. The primary asset type. target — Valid URL or hostname The main entry point URL. criticality ✅ Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational Risk tier classification. Owner Email — Valid email address The assigned owner account. description — Text Description or notes. scope — Semicolon-separated IPs/CIDRs Target definitions (specifically for network assets).

Validation Guard: The presence of any unknown columns will reject the entire file to prevent malformed data imports.

docs.title: CSV Import Process
docs.text:
1. Click Import CSV in the toolbar of the Assets list page.
  2. Select your formatted CSV file and click Upload + import.
  3. Security Virus Scan: The platform automatically scans all uploaded CSVs. On a cold start, this scanning queue can take up to 15 minutes. You will see a "still scanning" message.
  4. Queue Processing: Once cleared by the scanner, the file is processed as a background job.
  5. Real-time Status: The progress panel displays the running tally of successfully imported rows and failed rows.
  6. Error Reporting: Any malformed or duplicate rows are reported in an error table showing the row number, error code, field, and reason. Successful rows are committed immediately, so a few bad rows will not block the import of valid records.

← Previous: Overview | Next: Asset Detail

docs.title: Edit Asset
docs.text: Only users with Client Admin or Client TPM privileges can edit assets. This guide explains how to update existing asset configurations and define boundaries for security testing.

docs.title: 1. Accessing the Edit Interface
docs.text:
To edit an asset:

  1. Navigate to the Assets module in the sidebar.
  2. Click on the name of the asset you want to update to open its Asset Details page.
  3. In the top-right header, click the Edit button.

docs.title: 2. Editable Fields & Structure
docs.text:
The page is titled Edit asset name and is organised into numbered sections, the same way as the asset creation form:

Section What you can update 1. Basic information The asset name (must remain unique), the criticality level, and the rich-text Description (what the asset is, who uses it, and any special context testers should know). 2. Asset type Add or remove types (pick up to 3). Deselecting a type removes its scope section. 3. Scope details The type-specific targets and optional file uploads: URL lists, Postman collections, OpenAPI / Swagger specs, APK / IPA files, diagrams, and the network target IP/CIDR table. 4. Credential sets Upload a credential file for bug bounty / VDP researchers. This section appears only if your role can manage this asset's credentials.

docs.title: 3. How Credentials Work on the Edit Page
docs.text:
Test credentials contain sensitive secrets that are encrypted at rest, so they are handled differently from the other fields:

  • The Credential sets section (section 4) lets you upload a credential file. Uploads are saved immediately and are independent of the Save changes button.
  • Existing secrets are never shown back on the edit form. Viewing (revealing), adding, and deleting test accounts is managed under the Credentials tab on the Asset Details page.

The Edit Asset page has no Rules of engagement fields. In-scope and out-of-scope notes are provided when you request a pentest engagement or a Bug Bounty / VDP program. See Create Engagement and Request a Program.

docs.title: 4. Saving Changes
docs.text:
Once updates are complete, click Save changes in the sticky footer, or Cancel to return to the Asset Details page without saving. If any file uploads fail during the save process, you will receive a notification prompting you to retry uploading that specific file.

← Previous: Asset Detail | Next: Findings

docs.title: 1. What an "asset" is and why it matters
docs.text:
In Tri-Netra, an asset is a single testable target that belongs to your organisation — a web application, an API, a mobile app, a network range, a cloud environment, and so on. It is the root record that every security activity hangs off:

  • A PTaaS engagement (a scheduled penetration test) is always scoped to one or more assets.
  • A Bug Bounty program advertises an asset (or set of assets) for researchers to test.
  • An ASM scan (attack-surface monitoring) discovers and watches an asset's exposed surface.

Think of your asset inventory as the foundation of all your security testing. By defining your assets clearly (with the exact web links, IP ranges, or applications to test), our security team can work efficiently without guessing what is in scope. Setting the correct business importance (criticality) for each asset also ensures that any discovered vulnerabilities are prioritized and fixed correctly. Investing a small amount of time up front to set up your assets accurately makes all your future testing faster and more effective.

Mental model: Think of an asset as a "product record" for security. It has identity (name, type), risk classification (criticality), a precise definition of what's in bounds (scope contract), optional secrets testers need (credentials), and a lifecycle (active → archived).

docs.title: 2. What each client role can do (and why)
docs.text:
Asset permissions are enforced centrally by the platform's authorization service. That means the rules below hold no matter how you reach a page.

Action Client Admin Client TPM Client Viewer Why View / search list ✅ ✅ ✅ Everyone in your org needs situational awareness. Open detail (metadata) ✅ ✅ ✅ Reviewing scope/criticality is read-only. Export list to CSV ✅ ✅ ✅ Export is a client-side dump of what you can already see. Create / Edit / Import ✅ ✅ ❌ These change the inventory — a write surface. Clone ✅ ✅ ❌ Clone creates a new record (same surface as create). Archive / Restore ✅ ✅ ❌ Lifecycle changes are writes. View asset credentials ❌ ❌ ❌ Secrets are gated by a separate policy; clients don't read them back.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Click Assets in the left sidebar menu.

docs.title: 3. The Assets list — every control explained
docs.text: The list is your inventory dashboard: what exists, how risky it is, and whether it's actively being tested.

docs.title: Toolbar (top-right)
docs.text:
Control Type What it does Expected result Density toggle Toggle Switches row height between comfortable and compact. Table redraws denser/looser; purely visual, nothing is saved. Export CSV Button Serialises the currently loaded rows to a file. Browser downloads assets-export-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv with columns for name, target type, target URL, criticality, owner email, and description. Disabled when the list is empty. Import CSV Button → page Opens the bulk-import workflow. Opens the bulk import page. (Client Admin / Client TPM only.) New asset Button → page Opens the create form. Opens the create asset form. (Client Admin / Client TPM only.)

Why Export is available to everyone but Import isn't: Exporting only reveals data you already have permission to see, so it's safe for Client Viewer. Importing writes new records, so it's restricted to admins/TPMs.

docs.title: Filter bar
docs.text:
All filters combine (AND logic) and narrow the table in place:

Filter Type Values Use case Search Text Matches asset name Jump to a known asset quickly. Type Dropdown Web App, API, Mobile (Android/iOS), Network, Cloud, Hardware, Thick Client, IoT/Embedded, Telecom, Physical, Other "Show me only our APIs." Criticality Dropdown Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational "Which crown-jewel assets do we have?" State Dropdown Active / Inactive / Archived Find retired assets, or hide them. Clear Button — Appears once any filter is set; resets all filters at once.

Filters are held in memory and reset when you navigate away — they are not written to the URL. This is intentional so a shared link never leaks your filtering intent.

docs.title: Table columns
docs.text:
Column Meaning Name The asset's unique name in your org. Click to open its detail page. Type One or more coloured badges. An asset can carry up to 3 types (e.g. a product that is both a Web App and an API). Criticality Colour-coded pill from Critical (red) → Informational (blue). Drives triage priority. State Active / Inactive / Archived. Owner The person accountable for the asset, or — if unassigned. Engagements How many engagements (active or historical) reference this asset — a quick signal of how heavily tested it is. Created When the asset record was created.

Empty state: With no assets (or none matching your filters) you'll see a prompt with Add asset and Import CSV buttons instead of a table.

docs.title: Best practices & Tips
docs.text:
• Prioritize Critical Assets: Make sure your highest criticality assets are clearly named and fully documented first.
  • Consistent Naming: Use a naming convention that matches your internal systems (e.g., brand-app-prod, payments-api-staging) so team members instantly recognize the target.

← Previous: Dashboard | Next: Create Asset

docs.title: Request a Bug Bounty Program
docs.text:
Who can do this: Client Admin only. Client TPM and Client Viewer do not see the New program button.

Clients request a program rather than launching one directly. You fill in the program details and submit a request. SecurityBoat reviews it, sets the reward amounts for paid programs, and then schedules or activates it. You can follow every request under My Program Requests.

flowchart LR
    A[Choose program type] --> B[Fill in program details]
    B --> C[Preview]
    C --> D[Submit request]
    D --> E([Requested])
    E -->|approved| F([Approved])
    E -->|declined| G([Rejected])
    F --> H([Scheduled / Active])

docs.title: Step 1 — Choose the program type
docs.text:
Go to BB Program in the sidebar and click New program (or Request a program on the My Program Requests page).

Card Choose when… VDP — Vulnerability Disclosure Program You want a responsible-disclosure channel. Researchers earn recognition (swag + Hall of Fame), not money. Bug Bounty — Paid Bug Bounty Program You want severity-tiered cash rewards. Marked Paid plan.

Free plan: the Bug Bounty card is visible but disabled, with the note "Not available on the Free plan — Bug Bounty is a Paid-tier capability." Free-plan organisations can request VDP programs. Contact your CSM to upgrade.

The program type cannot be changed after the request is submitted.

docs.title: Step 2 — Fill in the program details
docs.text: The page is titled Request Bug Bounty program (or Request VDP program). Fields marked with a red asterisk (*) are required.

docs.title: Organisation & Basics
docs.text:
Field Required What to enter Program name ✅ A clear, descriptive name (e.g., Acme Storefront Bounty). At least 3 characters. Description ✅ What the program covers and why. Researchers read this first. Program type — Filled in from Step 1. Read-only.

About the editor: Description and the other long-text fields use a rich-text editor with a formatting toolbar (bold, italic, headings, lists, quotes, code blocks, links). You can switch to Markdown mode or use Preview to check the result.

docs.title: Scope & Policy
docs.text:
Field Required What to enter In-scope assets ✅ Select one or more of your active assets. Only assets registered in the Assets module appear. If the list is empty, add assets there first. In scope — What researchers may test on those assets — endpoints, environments, and vulnerability classes that qualify. Example: Authenticated flows on staging, API v2 endpoints, OWASP Top 10 classes. Out of scope — What is explicitly excluded. Reports about these items do not qualify for a reward. Example: DoS/DDoS, social engineering, third-party SaaS subdomains, rate-limit reports. Rules of engagement ✅ Testing windows, rate limits, and prohibited techniques. Safe-harbor policy — A Show safe-harbor policy toggle. The policy text itself is the platform's standard safe-harbor statement, managed centrally by SecurityBoat. When the toggle is on, the program shows a Safe Harbor badge and the policy on its Scope tab.

Why scope matters: researchers can only be held to rules you have written down. Clear in-scope and out-of-scope notes reduce noise and disputes.

docs.title: Schedule & Visibility
docs.text: Field Required What to enter Start date ✅ When the program should open. End date — Disabled until you pick a start date. Leave blank for a continuous program. It must be on or after the start date. Visibility — Public — all eligible researchers or Private — invite-only researchers. Enable Hall of Fame — Shows the top researchers on the program's Overview tab. Recommended.

docs.title: Management Model
docs.text: Option What it means SB-Managed SecurityBoat assigns a TPM and provides triage support. Requires a Paid plan. Self-Managed Your team runs triage. No SecurityBoat TPM is assigned.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• Bug Bounty: you do not enter reward amounts. A banner explains that bounty amounts are set by your SecurityBoat CSM, who prices each severity tier (P1–P5) before the program goes live.
  • VDP: a banner explains that VDP programs are recognition-based — valid reports earn swag and Hall of Fame placement, with no monetary reward table.

docs.title: Step 3 — Preview and submit
docs.text:
1. Click Preview to see how the program page will look once approved. The preview shows the same header, KPI tiles, and tabs as a real program. Nothing is submitted until you click Submit request.
  2. Click Close to return to the form, or Submit request to send it.

The Preview and Submit request buttons stay disabled until you have entered a program name and selected at least one in-scope asset.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
1. Your request appears under My Program Requests with the status Requested — "Awaiting review by your SecurityBoat team."
  2. SecurityBoat reviews the request. For Bug Bounty programs, your CSM also sets the reward amounts.
  3. The request is either:
    • Approved — the program page becomes available. It is then Scheduled (goes live on the start date) or Active.
    • Rejected — the reviewer's reason is shown under My Program Requests. Adjust the details and submit a new request.
  4. Once Active:
    • Public programs are open to all eligible researchers.
    • Private programs are open to invited researchers. On a Self-Managed Private program, a Client Admin can invite researchers from the Team tab. On an SB-Managed program, SecurityBoat handles invitations.
  5. Monitor the Findings tab as reports arrive.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No "New program" button Only Client Admin can request programs. The Bug Bounty card is disabled Your organisation is on the Free plan. Choose VDP or contact your CSM to upgrade. SB-Managed is disabled SB-Managed requires a Paid plan. Choose Self-Managed or contact your CSM. The asset list is empty You have no active assets. Add or reactivate an asset in the Assets module first. End date cannot be selected Pick a start date first. Submit request stays disabled Enter a program name and select at least one in-scope asset.

← Previous: Overview | Next: My Program Requests →

docs.title: Changing a Bug Bounty Program
docs.text:
Who edits programs: SecurityBoat (your CSM or assigned TPM). Client roles do not have an Edit button on the program page.

Once a program request is submitted, its settings are managed by SecurityBoat. This keeps scope, rewards, and dates consistent with what researchers have been told, and every change is recorded in the program's Activity tab.

docs.title: How to request a change
docs.text:
1. Open the program and note what needs to change (for example, a new in-scope asset, an updated out-of-scope note, a new end date, or a reward change).
  2. Contact your CSM, or post the request in the program Chat with the Client only audience so only your team and SecurityBoat see it.
  3. SecurityBoat applies the change. It appears in the Activity tab, and scope or reward changes are usually announced to researchers in the Updates tab.

docs.title: What can be changed
docs.text:
Area Examples Basics Program name, description Scope & policy In-scope assets, In scope / Out of scope notes, rules of engagement, safe-harbor display Schedule & visibility Start date, end date, Public / Private, Hall of Fame Rewards (Bug Bounty) P1–P5 amounts and currency Lifecycle Activate, deactivate (pause), reactivate, or end the program

Program type (VDP or Bug Bounty) cannot be changed. To switch type, request a new program.

docs.title: If your request was declined
docs.text: A declined request cannot be edited. Read the reason under My Program Requests, adjust the details, and submit a new request.

docs.title: Things you can manage yourself
docs.text: Task Where Invite or remove researchers on a Self-Managed Private program (Client Admin) Team tab Triage findings on a Self-Managed program (Client Admin, Client TPM) Findings tab Approve rewards on a Self-Managed Bug Bounty program (Client Admin) Payouts tab Map the program to Jira (Client Admin) Integrations tab

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• Visibility changes take effect immediately. Switching from Private to Public makes the program visible to all eligible researchers.
  • Scope changes should be announced to researchers through the Updates tab. Ask your CSM to post one.
  • All changes are audited in the Activity tab.

← Previous: Chat | Next: Hacktivity →

docs.title: My Program Requests
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who can request a program: Client Admin.

My Program Requests shows every Bug Bounty and VDP program your organisation has requested and where each one stands. It is the only place that shows the reviewer's reason when a request is declined, because a requested or declined program does not have a program page yet.

To open it, click My Program Requests in the sidebar.

docs.title: The requests table
docs.text:
Column What it shows Program The program name, with VDP or Bug Bounty underneath. Status The program state badge, a one-line explanation, and the reviewer's reason if the request was declined. Scope The number of in-scope assets. Starts The requested start date. Requested When the request was submitted. Reviewed When SecurityBoat reviewed it. (last column) Open once the program page is available. Before that, it shows the state name.

Client Admins also see a Request a program button at the top of the page. The table shows 10 requests per page.

docs.title: What each status means
docs.text:
Status Explanation shown on the page What you can do Requested Awaiting review by your SecurityBoat team. Wait for the review. The program page opens once the request is approved. Rejected Declined during review — see the reason below. Read the reason, adjust, and submit a new request. Scheduled Approved. It goes live on the start date. Click Open to review the program page. Active Live and accepting researcher submissions. Click Open to follow findings. Approved / Deactivated Approved but not currently accepting submissions. Click Open. Contact your CSM if you expected it to be live. Ended This program has finished. Click Open to read its history and findings. 
flowchart LR
    R([Requested]) --> A([Approved])
    R --> X([Rejected])
    A --> S([Scheduled]) --> L([Active])
    A --> L
    L --> E([Ended])

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix "No program requests yet" Nobody in your organisation has requested a program yet. No Open button The request is still Requested, or it was Rejected. The program page opens only after approval. No Request a program button Only Client Admin can request programs.

← Previous: Request a Program | Next: Program Detail →

docs.title: Bug Bounty — Overview
docs.text: Availability: The Bug Bounty module is subscription-gated. The BB Program, My Program Requests, Hacktivity, and Disclosure Requests entries appear in your sidebar only if your organisation has been onboarded for Bug Bounty. If they are missing, contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM).

docs.title: What is Bug Bounty?
docs.text:
A Bug Bounty program invites SecurityBoat's vetted community of security researchers to continuously test your assets and submit discovered vulnerabilities — typically in exchange for a reward.

Unlike a scheduled pentest where a fixed team tests within a defined window, a Bug Bounty program is ongoing and crowd-sourced: many researchers, working continuously, are paid or recognised per valid finding.

docs.title: Program types
docs.text: Type What it means for you Researcher incentive VDP — Vulnerability Disclosure Program Opens a responsible-disclosure channel so researchers can report issues. A good starting point for crowd-sourced security. Recognition only — swag, Hall of Fame listing, and reputation points. No monetary reward. Bug Bounty A paid program with defined scope and severity-tiered monetary rewards. Attracts deeper testing. Cash reward per valid finding, scaled to severity (P1–P5).

docs.title: Program visibility
docs.text: Visibility Who can find and join Public Any eligible researcher on the platform can see and participate. Private Only invited researchers can see and participate. Better for sensitive assets or early-stage programs.

docs.title: Management model
docs.text:
Every program shows a management badge in the program list, on the program page, and on each finding. Hover over the badge to read what it means.

Badge Who triages findings SB-Managed SecurityBoat's team reviews and manages the findings for this program. A SecurityBoat TPM is assigned. Self-Managed Your own team reviews and manages the findings. SecurityBoat is not involved in triage.

docs.title: Plan: Paid vs Free
docs.text:
What you can request depends on your organisation's plan:

Paid plan Free plan VDP programs ✅ ✅ Bug Bounty (paid reward) programs ✅ ❌ Public and Private visibility ✅ ✅ SB-Managed programs ✅ ❌ Self-Managed programs ✅ ✅

On the Free plan the Bug Bounty card is still shown when you create a program, but it is disabled with a note that Bug Bounty is a Paid-plan capability. Contact your CSM to upgrade.

docs.title: How it differs from a Pentest
docs.text:
PTaaS Pentest Bug Bounty Duration Fixed window (e.g., 2 weeks) Ongoing — no end date required Researchers Assigned team Open or invited crowd Scope Defined per engagement Defined per program When you see findings After SecurityBoat verifies them As soon as a researcher submits them (from New onward) Cost model Engagement fee Per valid finding (or recognition-based)

Bug Bounty findings also appear in your unified Findings list with the source BUG BOUNTY.

docs.title: What each client role can do
docs.text:
Action Client Admin Client TPM Client Viewer View programs, program detail tabs, and Hacktivity ✅ ✅ ✅ View My Program Requests ✅ ✅ ✅ Request a new program ✅ ❌ ❌ Invite / remove researchers on a Self-Managed Private program ✅ ❌ ❌ Act on findings (confirm, start fixing, submit for retest) ✅ ✅ ❌ Triage findings on a Self-Managed program ✅ ✅ ❌ Approve rewards on a Self-Managed Bug Bounty program ✅ ❌ ❌ View Disclosure Requests ✅ ✅ ❌ Approve or reject a disclosure request ✅ ❌ ❌ Send messages in program Chat ✅ ✅ ❌

Program settings are managed by SecurityBoat. Clients request a program and SecurityBoat reviews, approves, schedules, and edits it. If a live program needs a change (scope, dates, rewards), ask your CSM.

docs.title: The program lifecycle
docs.text:
A program you request moves through these states. The same lifecycle applies to Bug Bounty and VDP programs.

flowchart LR
    R([Requested]) -->|SecurityBoat approves| A([Approved])
    R -->|SecurityBoat declines| X([Rejected])
    A --> S([Scheduled])
    A --> L([Active])
    S -->|start date reached| L
    L -->|paused| D([Deactivated])
    D -->|re-activated| L
    L -->|end date or closed| E([Ended])
    D --> E
State What it means for you Requested You submitted the request. SecurityBoat is reviewing it. Rejected The request was declined. The reviewer's reason is shown under My Program Requests. Approved SecurityBoat approved the request. The program exists but is not accepting submissions yet. Scheduled The program goes live automatically on its start date. Active Live. Researchers can test and submit findings. Deactivated Paused. Existing findings, scope, and updates stay readable, but new findings are not accepted. Ended The program has finished (on its end date, or closed by SecurityBoat). Read-only.

Only Active programs accept new findings. Only Active Public programs are listed in the public program directory.

docs.title: Bug Bounty Programs list
docs.text:
Click BB Program in the sidebar to open the Programs list.

Element What it shows KPI tiles Total programs, Active, and Awaiting review (requests still being reviewed). Type tabs All Programs, VDP, Bug Bounty. State filter All States plus one pill per state (Requested, Rejected, Approved, Scheduled, Active, Deactivated, Ended). Search Search by program name. Table columns Program, Client, Type, Management (SB-Managed / Self-Managed), Visibility, Status, Findings. New program Client Admin only. Opens the program request form.

Your filters and page number are kept in the page address, so opening a program and pressing Back returns you to the same filtered page. The list shows 10 programs per page.

Other Bug Bounty pages in the sidebar:

  • My Program Requests — every program your organisation has requested and where it stands. See My Program Requests.
  • Hacktivity — the public feed of disclosed, resolved reports.
  • Disclosure Requests — researcher requests to publicly disclose a finding (Client Admin and Client TPM).

docs.title: How it all fits together
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Client Admin requests a program] --> B[SecurityBoat reviews the request]
    B -->|Approved| C[Program is scheduled or activated]
    B -->|Rejected| Z[Reason shown in My Program Requests]
    C --> D[Researchers test in-scope assets]
    D --> E[Researcher submits a report]
    E --> F{Management model}
    F -->|SB-Managed| G[SecurityBoat triages]
    F -->|Self-Managed| H[Your team triages]
    G --> I[Finding verified]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Your team fixes it and submits for retest]
    J --> K[Fix confirmed: Resolved]
    K --> L[Optional: researcher requests disclosure]
    L --> M[TPM review, then your approval]
    M --> N[Published on Hacktivity]

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Start with a VDP if you are new to crowd-sourced security. It opens a disclosure channel without monetary commitments.
  • Use Private visibility for new programs or sensitive assets.
  • Define scope clearly — fill in the In scope and Out of scope fields so researchers know what qualifies.
  • Act on verified findings promptly — move them to Fix in Progress and then submit them for retest.
  • Review disclosure requests promptly — timely disclosure builds researcher trust.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / Fix No Bug Bounty entries in the sidebar Your organisation is not onboarded for Bug Bounty. Contact your CSM. No "New program" button Only Client Admin can request programs. The Bug Bounty card is disabled when creating a program Your organisation is on the Free plan, which supports VDP programs only. Contact your CSM to upgrade. My requested program has no page to open A program page opens only after the request is approved. Track it under My Program Requests. There is no Edit button on the program Program settings are edited by SecurityBoat. Contact your CSM with the change you need. Researchers say they cannot submit findings The program is not Active (it may be Approved, Scheduled, Deactivated, or Ended).

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
Guide What it covers Request a Program Step-by-step guide to requesting a VDP or Bug Bounty program My Program Requests Tracking your requests and reading review outcomes Program Detail Header, lifecycle stepper, KPIs, tab navigation, and the Overview tab Scope In-scope assets, scope notes, rules of engagement, safe harbor, and test credentials Rewards Severity-tiered reward structure and recognition model Findings Findings submitted to this program and their lifecycle Team Invited researchers on Private programs Payouts Reward approvals, statuses, and invoices Leaderboard Researcher ranking by reputation Collaborators Every researcher who has contributed to this program Chat Messaging channel for program communication Changing a Program How program changes are handled

← Previous: ASM Subdomains | Next: Request a Program →

docs.title: Program Detail
docs.text:
The program detail page is your command centre for a Bug Bounty or VDP program. It shows the program's lifecycle, configuration, findings, rewards, and team in one place.

To open a program, go to BB Program in the sidebar and click any program in the list. You can also click Open next to an approved request under My Program Requests.

docs.title: Page header
docs.text:
The header identifies the program at a glance:

Element What it shows Program code A short reference code in a pill badge (e.g. BB-ACS-01 or VDP-ACS-01). Status The current state: Requested, Approved, Scheduled, Active, Deactivated, Ended, or Rejected. Visibility Public or Private. Type VDP (shield icon) or Bug Bounty (lightning icon). Management badge SB-Managed or Self-Managed. Hover or focus the badge to read what it means. Safe Harbor badge Shown when the program displays a safe-harbor policy. Program name and Organisation The full program name and your organisation.

There is no Edit button for client roles. Program settings are edited by SecurityBoat — see Changing a Program.

docs.title: Lifecycle stepper
docs.text:
Below the header, a full-width stepper shows where the program is in its lifecycle:

flowchart LR
    R([Requested]) --> A([Approved]) --> S([Scheduled]) --> L([Active]) --> E([Ended])
  • Completed steps are checked and the current step is highlighted.
  • If the request was declined, the first step reads Rejected, and a Request declined box under the stepper shows who declined it and why.
  • If the program is paused, the Active step reads Deactivated and is shown in amber.

docs.title: Deactivated or ended programs
docs.text:
When a program is Deactivated or Ended, a notice appears under the header:

This program is deactivated. (or This program is closed.) New findings are not being accepted. Existing findings, scope and updates remain available.

docs.title: KPI tiles
docs.text: Tile Bug Bounty shows VDP shows Total bounties paid Cumulative amount paid out Recognition — VDP — swag + HoF Reports received Total findings submitted to this program Same Active since Program start date Same

docs.title: Tab navigation
docs.text:
Click any tab to switch views. The selected tab is kept in the page address, so you can share a direct link to it.

Tab Who sees it Guide Overview All client roles This page Scope All client roles Scope → Credential requests All client roles (actions only on Self-Managed programs) Scope → Test credentials Rewards All client roles Rewards → Findings All client roles Findings → Team Private programs only Team → Payouts All client roles Payouts → Activity All client roles This page Leaderboard All client roles Leaderboard → Collaborators All client roles Collaborators → Updates All client roles This page Chat All client roles Chat → Integrations All client roles (Jira setup: Client Admin) This page

docs.title: Program details
docs.text: Field Description Program ID The program's reference code Type VDP or Bug Bounty Status The current state Visibility Public or Private Organisation Your organisation name Managed by SB-Managed or Self-Managed Start date When the program opens End date Close date, or Continuous if open-ended Hall of Fame Enabled or Disabled Reward structure P1–P5 reward chips (Bug Bounty), or VDP — swag & Hall of Fame recognition

docs.title: Management model
docs.text:
A card repeats the management badge with a one-line explanation:

  • SB-Managed — SecurityBoat's team reviews and manages the findings for this program.
  • Self-Managed — The client's own team reviews and manages the findings. SecurityBoat is not involved in triage.

docs.title: Program stats
docs.text:
A five-cell grid counts the program's findings:

Cell What it counts Total All findings submitted Triage Findings awaiting review Accepted Findings confirmed valid and being remediated Resolved Findings that have been fixed Discarded Findings closed as invalid, duplicate, or not applicable

docs.title: Hall of Fame (if enabled)
docs.text: The top three researchers appear as podium cards. Filter by Today, This Week, or All Time. Until findings are accepted, the section reads: "No researchers on the leaderboard yet. Top contributors will appear once findings are accepted."

docs.title: Activity tab
docs.text:
The Activity tab is a chronological log of everything that happens on the program, with the time and the person who did it. Events include:

  • The request being submitted, approved, or declined
  • State changes (scheduled, activated, deactivated, ended)
  • Scope changes
  • Team invitations and removals
  • Finding submissions and state changes
  • Payout approvals

When there is no activity yet, the tab reads: "No activity yet. Events will appear here as the program is managed."

docs.title: Updates tab
docs.text:
The Updates tab holds program announcements posted by SecurityBoat — scope changes, reward changes, testing-window restrictions, and policy updates. Each update shows its title, author, date, and content.

Clients can read updates but not post them. Ask your CSM if you want an announcement posted.

docs.title: Integrations tab
docs.text:
If your organisation has connected Jira, a Client Admin can map this program to a Jira project (Set up Jira) and then sync selected findings from the Findings tab.

If Jira is not connected yet, connect it first under Integrations in the sidebar. See the Integrations guide.

← Previous: My Program Requests | Next: Scope →

docs.title: Program Chat
docs.text:
Who can read: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who can send: Client Admin and Client TPM. Client Viewer is read-only.

The Chat tab is a messaging channel for this program. Your team, SecurityBoat staff, and (on Private programs) invited researchers can communicate in one place instead of over email.

On Public programs, researchers do not have access to the program Chat. It is used by your team and SecurityBoat.

docs.title: Choosing who sees a message
docs.text:
Before sending, pick the audience. As a client you can choose:

Audience Who can read it When to use Everyone Everyone in this chat — your team, SecurityBoat staff, and researchers who have chat access Scope clarifications and program-wide announcements Client only Your team plus SecurityBoat staff (SB Admin, CSM, TPM). Researchers cannot see it Discussing findings, payouts, or changes you do not want researchers to see

Each message shows a badge with its audience, plus the sender's name, role, and time. You always see your own messages. Messages from audiences your role cannot read are not shown to you.

docs.title: Mentioning people
docs.text: Type @ in the message box to mention a participant. Only people who can read the message can be mentioned, and they are notified.

docs.title: How to send a message
docs.text:
1. Open the Chat tab on the program.
  2. Choose the audience: Everyone or Client only.
  3. Type your message. The editor supports rich text and Markdown, with a Preview option.
  4. Send. The chat updates in real time.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use Everyone for program-wide updates so invited researchers are informed.
  • Use Client only for internal discussion with SecurityBoat — researchers will not see it.
  • Do not share sensitive details with Everyone.
  • Use @mentions to get a specific person's attention.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix I cannot send messages You are Client Viewer (read-only). A researcher cannot see my message It was sent as Client only, or the program is Public (researchers have no Chat on Public programs). I cannot @mention someone They cannot read a message with the selected audience. The chat is not updating Refresh the page. The chat reconnects automatically in most cases.

← Previous: Collaborators | Next: Changing a Program →

docs.title: Program Collaborators
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer.

The Collaborators tab lists every researcher who has contributed to this program in any capacity — submitting a finding, co-reporting, retesting, or assisting with triage.

docs.title: What you will see
docs.text:
Each collaborator row displays:

Column Description Researcher Display name and username Reputation Points Total points accumulated on this program Contribution breakdown Number of reports versus collaborations Contact Link to view the researcher's public profile

docs.title: Collaborators vs. Team
docs.text:
Do not confuse this with the Team tab:

Tab Shows Team Researchers invited to a Private program (may not have submitted yet) Collaborators Researchers who have contributed — submitted, co-reported, or retested (all programs)

On a Public program, you will only see the Collaborators tab. On a Private program, you will see both tabs — Team for invited researchers and Collaborators for those who have actually submitted.

docs.title: Researcher profiles
docs.text:
Clicking Contact opens a researcher's public profile, which typically shows:

  • Researcher's display name and avatar
  • Overall platform reputation
  • Areas of expertise (e.g., web, mobile, API, cloud)
  • Number of findings submitted across all programs

This is useful for identifying researchers you may want to invite to future private programs or engage for deeper testing.

docs.title: When the tab is empty
docs.text:
If no researchers have contributed yet, the tab shows: "No collaborators yet. Researchers appear here once they submit findings to this program." This is expected for newly created programs.

← Previous: Leaderboard | Next: Chat →

docs.title: Program Findings
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who can act on findings: Client Admin and Client TPM.

The Findings tab lists every report submitted to this program, across every state of the lifecycle. Click a row to open the finding.

You can also see Bug Bounty findings across all your programs in the main Findings module. This tab is scoped to one program.

docs.title: KPI overview and sub-tabs
docs.text:
Tile What it counts Total findings All reports submitted to this program Awaiting triage New reports that need a triage decision In remediation Accepted findings that are being fixed Resolved Fixed findings, with the percentage of all findings

Two sub-tabs sit above the table: All Findings and Triage (n), which shows only reports still awaiting triage.

docs.title: Findings table
docs.text:
Column Description Finding Title and finding ID Severity P1 Critical to P5 Informational State Current lifecycle state, plus a closure label (e.g. Duplicate, Not Applicable) when one applies Researcher Who submitted the report Jira The linked Jira issue, if synced Submitted Submission date Actions Disclosure status: Requested while a disclosure request is under review, or Published once it is live on Hacktivity

A Client Admin whose organisation has connected Jira can select findings with the checkboxes and sync them to the mapped Jira project. If the program is not mapped yet, use Set up Jira.

docs.title: When you see a finding
docs.text: Bug Bounty findings are visible to your team from the moment a researcher submits them (state New). You never see a researcher's unsubmitted Draft.

docs.title: The finding lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    N([New]) --> T([Triaged])
    T -->|SB-Managed only| P([Pending Client Validation])
    P --> V([Verified])
    T --> V
    V --> F([Fix in Progress])
    F --> R([Retesting])
    R -->|fix confirmed| D([Resolved])
    R -->|retest failed| F

A report can also be closed from any open state as Duplicate or Not Applicable, and may end as Informative or Spam.

State What it means New Submitted and awaiting initial review. Triaged Initial review done; awaiting detailed validation. Pending Client Validation SB-Managed programs only. SecurityBoat has referred the report to your team to confirm. Verified Confirmed as a legitimate, reproducible security issue. Fix in Progress Your team is working on the fix. Retesting Your fix is deployed and awaiting verification. Resolved Fixed and successfully retested. Duplicate Already reported, or covered by an existing report. Not Applicable Does not show a valid security issue within the program's scope or acceptance criteria. Informative Useful information that does not qualify for remediation or a reward. Spam Irrelevant, abusive, or not a legitimate submission.

docs.title: Who does what
docs.text:
The steps depend on the program's management model.

Step SB-Managed program Self-Managed program Mark as triaged (New → Triaged) SecurityBoat Client Admin / Client TPM Refer to client for validation (Triaged → Pending Client Validation) SecurityBoat Not used Confirm as verified (Pending Client Validation → Verified) Client Admin / Client TPM Not used Verify finding (Triaged → Verified) SecurityBoat Client Admin / Client TPM Acknowledge and start fixing (Verified → Fix in Progress) Client Admin / Client TPM Client Admin / Client TPM Submit fix for retesting (Fix in Progress → Retesting) Client Admin / Client TPM Client Admin / Client TPM Confirm fix verified (resolve) (Retesting → Resolved) SecurityBoat Client Admin / Client TPM Retest failed — send back to fix (Retesting → Fix in Progress) SecurityBoat Client Admin / Client TPM Request more information / Close as duplicate / Close as not applicable / Reopen (clear closure) SecurityBoat Client Admin / Client TPM Provide requested information Client Admin / Client TPM, the researcher, or SecurityBoat Same

Client Viewer can read findings but has no actions.

Actions are taken from the State actions panel on the finding detail page. See Findings for how the panel works. Closing as duplicate, closing as not applicable, reopening, and sending a failed retest back need a comment of at least 20 characters. Requesting or providing information needs at least 10 characters.

docs.title: Disclosure
docs.text: Once a finding is Resolved (or closed as Not Applicable), the researcher who submitted it can request public disclosure. The request is reviewed by the TPM and then by your team under Disclosure Requests. The Actions column shows Requested while it is under review and Published once it is live.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix A researcher says they submitted a finding but I cannot see it It is still a Draft on their side. Drafts are visible only to the researcher. I have no State actions You are Client Viewer, or no action is available to your role in the finding's current state (for example, triage on an SB-Managed program is done by SecurityBoat). There is no Pending Client Validation step The program is Self-Managed. Your team verifies findings directly. No Jira column or checkboxes Only Client Admin manages Jira, and Jira must be connected and mapped to this program.

← Previous: Rewards | Next: Team →

docs.title: Program Leaderboard
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer.

The Leaderboard tab ranks researchers who have had findings accepted on this program by their reputation points. It is a competitive, gamified view that celebrates top contributors.

docs.title: How points are earned
docs.text:
Points are awarded per accepted vulnerability based on its severity (P1 Critical earns the most, P5 Informational the least). The points per severity are set platform-wide by SecurityBoat and are the same on every program.

A researcher's score on this program is the sum of the points from all their accepted findings here.

docs.title: What the leaderboard shows
docs.text:
Each researcher row displays:

Column Description Rank Medal icon (🥇🥈🥉) for the top three; numeric rank for everyone else Researcher Display name and username Reputation Points Total points accumulated from accepted findings Rewards Earned Total bounty value earned (Bug Bounty programs only) Accepted Vulnerabilities Total count of accepted findings

docs.title: Time filters
docs.text:
You can filter the leaderboard view by time period:

Filter Shows Today Rankings based on findings accepted today This Week Rankings based on findings accepted this week All Time Cumulative rankings since the program launched

docs.title: Hall of Fame
docs.text: When the Hall of Fame setting is enabled on the program (set during creation), the top three researchers also appear as podium cards on the Overview tab of the program detail page.

docs.title: When the leaderboard is empty
docs.text: If no researchers have had findings accepted yet, the tab shows: "No researchers on the leaderboard yet. Researchers appear here once their findings are accepted." This is normal for new programs — the leaderboard fills up as researchers submit and your findings are triaged.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Enable Hall of Fame — it is a zero-cost way to motivate researchers through public recognition.
  • Use the leaderboard to spot trends — a researcher consistently finding P1/P2 issues may be worth inviting to private programs.
  • Do not use leaderboard rank alone to judge researcher quality — some excellent researchers may submit fewer but higher-quality findings.

← Previous: Payouts | Next: Collaborators →

docs.title: Program Payouts
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who approves: depends on the management model (see below).

The Payouts tab tracks the reward for every payable finding on the program. Findings appear here once they are verified. For VDP programs, the tab shows reputation points instead of money.

docs.title: Bug Bounty programs
docs.text: The tab header reads Payouts for program name with a running Total. A line underneath explains who approves on this program.

docs.title: Who approves
docs.text: Management model How a reward is approved SB-Managed SecurityBoat sets the reward amount and approves it. Your team does not need to act. Self-Managed Your team sets the reward amount when it verifies the finding, and a Client Admin approves first. SecurityBoat then gives the final approval.

docs.title: Reward status flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    V([Verified]) -->|Self-Managed: Client Admin approves| C([Awaiting SB Admin Approval])
    C --> A([Approved by SB Admin])
    V -->|SB-Managed: SecurityBoat approves| A
    A --> PI([Payment Initiated]) --> TA([Transaction Approved]) --> PD([Payment Done])
Status What it means Verified The finding is verified and the reward is waiting for approval. Awaiting SB Admin Approval Self-Managed only. Your Client Admin approved the reward; SecurityBoat's final approval is pending. Approved by SB Admin The reward is approved. The invoice becomes available. Payment Initiated SecurityBoat has started the payment to the researcher. Transaction Approved The payment transaction is approved. Payment Done The researcher has been paid. TDS Tax deducted at source has been recorded for the payment. Needs review The payout needs attention from SecurityBoat.

docs.title: Payouts table
docs.text: Column Description Finding Finding title and ID Researcher Who submitted it Severity P1 Critical to P5 Info Amount The reward amount Status The current reward status (see above) Invoice Invoice number with a download link, once the reward is approved Action Client Admin on Self-Managed programs: an Approve button while the reward is awaiting your approval

docs.title: Approving a reward (Client Admin, Self-Managed programs)
docs.text:
1. Make sure the finding has a reward amount. A reward with no amount cannot be approved.
  2. Click Approve on the row.
  3. In the Approve reward dialog, check the amount and researcher, and enter a reason (10–500 characters). The reason is kept with the payout history.
  4. Click Approve payout. The status changes to Awaiting SB Admin Approval.

docs.title: VDP programs
docs.text: VDP programs have no monetary payouts. The tab is titled Points for program name and shows the reputation points each accepted finding earned, with a total. Points per severity are set platform-wide by SecurityBoat.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Approve rewards promptly on Self-Managed programs. Rewards waiting too long frustrate researchers.
  • Check the severity before approving — the amount follows the program's reward table.
  • Keep invoice records for your finance and compliance needs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix I cannot see the Approve button The program is SB-Managed (SecurityBoat approves), you are not Client Admin, or the reward is already past your approval step. Approve is disabled The reward has no amount yet. Set it when verifying the finding, or contact your CSM. "No payouts yet" No findings on this program are verified yet. The amount seems wrong Check the Rewards tab and the finding's severity. Contact your CSM before approving if it needs correcting.

← Previous: Team | Next: Leaderboard →

docs.title: Program Rewards
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who sets rewards: SecurityBoat.

The Rewards tab shows what researchers earn for valid reports. The content depends on whether the program is a Bug Bounty or VDP.

docs.title: Bug Bounty programs
docs.text:
The Rewards tab shows a severity-tiered reward table:

Severity Label Typical examples P1 Critical Remote code execution, SQL injection, authentication bypass P2 High Access control bypass, stored XSS on critical endpoints, SSRF P3 Medium CSRF, sensitive information disclosure, reflected XSS P4 Low Minor configuration flaws P5 Informational Best-practice suggestions, low-risk observations

Each tier shows a single amount or a range (for example 100 - 1000) in the program's currency (INR, USD, EUR, or GBP).

Who sets the amounts: when you request a Bug Bounty program, you do not enter reward amounts. Your SecurityBoat CSM prices each severity tier before the program goes live. Ask your CSM if you want the amounts changed.

docs.title: How a reward is paid
docs.text: The reward for a finding is set when the finding is verified, based on its severity and the program's reward table. It then moves through the approval steps described in Payouts.

docs.title: VDP programs
docs.text:
VDP programs do not offer money. Valid reports earn:

  • Swag — merchandise as a token of appreciation
  • Hall of Fame placement — recognition on the program
  • Reputation points — platform-wide points that build a researcher's standing

VDP reputation points are set platform-wide by SecurityBoat and are the same for every program. They are not editable per program.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Competitive P1–P3 rewards attract higher-quality submissions.
  • P5 can be zero — informational findings are worth acknowledging but rarely justify a cash reward.
  • Review rewards periodically with your CSM as your program matures.

← Previous: Scope | Next: Findings →

docs.title: Program Scope
docs.text:
Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who can change it: SecurityBoat (see Changing a Program).

The Scope tab defines exactly what researchers are authorised to test under this program. Researchers must stay within this boundary.

docs.title: In-scope assets
docs.text:
Every asset linked to the program is shown as an expandable card. The card header shows the asset name, an Active or Inactive badge, the asset types (e.g. WEB APPLICATION, API WEB SERVICES), and the asset's criticality. Click a card to expand it.

The expanded card shows the asset details researchers work from:

Section What it contains Overview Description, types, criticality, and state of the asset Scope The targets registered on the asset — URLs, IP ranges, API endpoints, app identifiers, or other details for its type Attachments Files attached to the asset (read-only here)

If no assets are linked, the tab reads "No assets in scope."

Only assets registered in the Assets module can be in scope. Testing anything outside these assets is out of scope.

docs.title: Scope definition
docs.text: Field What it means In scope What researchers may test on the in-scope assets — endpoints, environments, and vulnerability classes that qualify Out of scope What is explicitly excluded. Reports about these items do not qualify for a reward

docs.title: Program overview
docs.text: Field Description Organisation Your organisation name In-scope assets Number of linked assets Program type VDP or Bug Bounty Description What the program covers Rules of engagement Testing windows, rate limits, prohibited techniques Safe harbor policy The platform's safe-harbor statement, when the program shows one. These programs also carry a Safe Harbor badge in the header

docs.title: Test credentials and credential requests
docs.text:
Some assets offer test accounts for researchers. Researchers request them from the Scope tab, and each request is reviewed before credentials are shared.

The program's Credential requests tab lists those requests (with views for pending requests, assignees, reported issues, requests waiting for credentials, and all requests).

Program type What client roles can do Self-Managed Client Admin and Client TPM can approve or reject requests and manage assignments. Client Viewer can view only. SB-Managed All client roles can view. SecurityBoat handles the requests.

Researchers never see credentials until a request is approved and a credential set is assigned. Revealed credentials hide automatically after a short time.

flowchart LR
    A[Researcher requests credentials] --> B([Pending review])
    B -->|approved| C([Approved, waiting for credentials])
    B -->|rejected| X([Rejected])
    C -->|set assigned| D([Credentials assigned])
    D --> E[Researcher reveals and tests]
    E -->|finished| F[Researcher releases access]

docs.title: Why scope matters
docs.text:
• Less noise: clear scope tells researchers where to focus.
  • Legal clarity: the safe-harbor policy and rules of engagement protect both parties.
  • Asset alignment: only registered assets can become test targets.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Asset list is empty No assets are linked. Ask your CSM to add assets to the program. An asset shows Inactive The asset was marked inactive in the Assets module. Reactivate it there, or ask your CSM to remove it from scope. A researcher tested something out of scope Out-of-scope reports are closed during triage. Make sure the Out of scope notes list what is excluded. No approve/reject buttons on Credential requests The program is SB-Managed, or you are Client Viewer.

← Previous: Program Detail | Next: Rewards →

docs.title: Program Team
docs.text:
Visibility: This tab appears on Private programs only. Public programs are open to every eligible researcher, so no invitations are needed.

Who can view: Client Admin, Client TPM, Client Viewer. Who can invite and remove researchers: Client Admin on a Self-Managed Private program. On an SB-Managed program, SecurityBoat manages the team.

The Team tab shows which researchers have been invited to this private program and whether they have accepted.

docs.title: The team list
docs.text:
Column Description Researcher Name and email Role Researcher or Lead Researcher Status Pending (invitation sent, not yet accepted) or Accepted Invited by Who sent the invitation Invited Date the invitation was sent

Researchers see the program and can submit findings once they accept the invitation. If nobody has been invited yet, the tab reads: "No researchers invited yet. Invite researchers to give them access to this private program."

docs.title: Inviting researchers (Client Admin, Self-Managed programs)
docs.text:
The Invite researchers card sits at the top of the tab.

  1. Open the Select researchers to invite… list.
  2. Type in the search box to find researchers by name or email.
  3. Tick one or more researchers. You can invite several at once. Researchers already on the program are not listed.
  4. Click Invite (the button shows the count, e.g. Invite (3), when several are selected).

Each invited researcher receives an invitation and appears in the list with the status Pending until they accept it from their Invites page.

flowchart LR
    A[Client Admin selects researchers] --> B[Invite]
    B --> C([Pending])
    C -->|researcher accepts| D([Accepted])
    D --> E[Researcher can view the program and submit findings]

docs.title: Removing a researcher
docs.text:
1. Click Remove on the researcher's row.
  2. A Remove researcher? dialog explains that the researcher will lose access to submit findings and view program details. You can re-invite them later if needed.
  3. Click Remove to confirm, or Cancel.

A removed researcher can no longer open the program. Findings they already submitted stay on the program.

docs.title: Team vs. Collaborators
docs.text: Tab Shows Team Researchers invited to a Private program, whether or not they have submitted anything Collaborators Researchers who have actually submitted findings (all programs)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No Invite researchers card You are not Client Admin, or the program is SB-Managed. Ask your CSM to invite researchers on SB-Managed programs. A researcher stays Pending They have not accepted the invitation yet. A researcher is missing from the picker They are already on the program, or their account is inactive.

← Previous: Findings | Next: Payouts →

docs.title: Create Engagement
docs.text:
From Pentest Engagements (or My Requests) click New engagement to open the pentest request form, titled Request a new pentest engagement. This is available to Client Admin and Client TPM.

"Pick the asset, scope, and preferred dates. The SecurityBoat team will review your request and either approve it or reject it with a reason."

docs.title: 1. The request form — section by section
What should we test?
docs.text:
The asset is the system under test. If it isn't listed, ask your admin to add it under Assets.

Field Required What to provide Asset ✅ The system to be tested. Only your organisation's active assets appear here. Engagement type ✅ The kind of test — Web Application, API / Web Services, Mobile, Network Infrastructure, Cloud, Hardware, IoT, and more.

docs.title: Scope & context
docs.text:
A short title plus any business-critical context the testers should know up-front.

Field Required What to provide Title ✅ 3–255 characters, e.g. "Q3 2026 production pentest". Description — Business context, special handling notes, or anything the testers should know.

docs.title: Rules of engagement
docs.text:
Define what testers should and should not target. Be as specific as possible — URLs, IPs, modules, or features.

Field Required What to provide In-scope — URLs, IPs, modules, or features the testers should focus on. Out-of-scope — URLs, IPs, modules, or features the testers must not target.

These notes appear on the engagement's Brief tab under Rules of engagement.

docs.title: Preferred dates
docs.text:
Approximate is fine — the SecurityBoat team will confirm the actual schedule with you.

Field Required What to provide Preferred start — The earliest date you'd like testing to begin. Preferred end — Your ideal end date. Disabled until you pick a start date, and it cannot be before the start date.

docs.title: 2. What happens after you submit
docs.text:
The What happens next panel beside the form summarises the flow:

flowchart LR
    A[Submit request] --> B[Review<br/>within 1 business day]
    B --> C[Scoping call]
    C --> D[Approval:<br/>Draft engagement]
    D --> E[Live testing]
    E --> F[Findings]
    F --> G[Client-approved report]
    G --> H[Final report]
    H --> I[Post-retest report]
  1. Review — SecurityBoat reviews scope and feasibility within 1 business day.
  2. Scoping call — a short call to confirm scope, environment, access, and dates.
  3. Approval — an approved request becomes a Draft engagement you can track end to end. A rejected request comes back with a reason.
  4. Delivery — Live testing → findings → report review → Final → Post-Retest report.

After you click Submit request, you're taken to the new engagement's page. Its state shows Requested until SecurityBoat reviews it. You can also follow it under My Requests.

docs.title: 3. After approval
docs.text: Once approved, use the engagement Chat to share anything the testers need — test accounts, VPN access, allow-listing details, or preferred testing hours. Test credentials can also be stored on the asset itself, where they are shared only with the testing team.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Fill in the rules of engagement — clear in-scope and out-of-scope notes prevent testers from touching systems you care about.
  • Give rich context in the Description to shorten the scoping call.
  • Make sure the asset is current before submitting.
  • Allow reasonable lead time (5+ business days) for team availability.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Asset dropdown is empty Your organisation has no active asset. Add or reactivate one under Assets. No "New engagement" button You're a Client Viewer (read-only). Preferred end can't be selected Pick a preferred start date first. Request was rejected Read the reason, adjust the details, and submit a new request.

← Previous: Overview | Next: Engagement Detail →

docs.title: Edit Engagement
docs.text: While your engagement is in Draft state (after your request is approved but before testing preparation begins), Client Admin and Client TPM can refine scoping details to ensure the testing team has everything they need.

docs.title: 1. What you can update during Draft
docs.text:
Detail How to provide it Additional scope context Use the engagement Chat to share credentials, VPN access details, preferred testing hours, or updated URLs. Preferred schedule adjustments If your timeline has changed, communicate the new preferred dates via Chat so the SecurityBoat team can adjust planning. Asset scope corrections If the wrong asset was selected or the asset's scope has changed, update the asset under Assets first, then notify your TPM in Chat.

Note: client users don't have a direct "Edit" button on the engagement — detailed field editing is handled by your SecurityBoat TPM. However, any information you provide during the Draft stage (via Chat or by updating your asset records) will be incorporated before testing begins.

docs.title: 2. What you can see but not edit
docs.text:
Once the engagement moves past Draft into active preparation or Live testing, the following details are locked and managed by the SecurityBoat team:

  • Title and description — set at request time.
  • Engagement type and testing approach — confirmed during the scoping call.
  • Schedule — finalized by SecurityBoat after the scoping call.
  • Rules of engagement (in-scope / out-of-scope) — you provide these in the request form; SecurityBoat confirms them during scoping and they are locked once testing begins.
  • Environment (Production, UAT, Staging, QA, or Development) — confirmed during scoping.

You can always view all of these on the Brief tab of the engagement detail page.

docs.title: 3. Communicating changes after Draft
docs.text:
If you need something changed after the engagement has moved past Draft:

  1. Open the engagement and go to the Chat tab.
  2. Describe what needs to change — be specific (e.g. "we've rotated the test credentials, here are the new ones" or "please exclude the /admin path — it's out of scope now").
  3. Your TPM will review and apply the change on your behalf.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Provide all credentials and access details early — ideally during Draft, before testing begins. Late access delivery delays the engagement.
  • Update your asset record if URLs or IP ranges changed — the engagement's scope references your asset, so keeping the asset current keeps the engagement scope correct.
  • Use Chat, not email — messages in engagement Chat are permanently attached to the engagement record and visible to the full SecurityBoat team working your pentest.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix I can't find a way to edit the engagement directly Client roles don't have a direct edit form — communicate changes to your TPM via Chat and they'll update the engagement on your behalf. My TPM hasn't applied my change Follow up in Chat. Changes communicated during active testing may take time to process depending on scope impact. The scope shown on Brief is outdated Update the asset under Assets, then notify your TPM so the engagement references are refreshed.

← Previous: Integrations | Back to: Overview

docs.title: 1. What an engagement is and how the PTaaS model works
docs.text:
An engagement is a scheduled penetration test of one of your assets, run by SecurityBoat's security team. "PTaaS" (Penetration Testing as a Service) means the whole lifecycle — requesting, scoping, testing, reporting, and retesting — happens on this platform instead of over email and PDFs.

Every engagement moves through the states below. The lifecycle stepper on each engagement shows where it stands.

flowchart LR
    RQ([Requested]) -->|approved| DR([Draft])
    RQ -->|rejected| CL([Closed])
    DR --> SC([Scoping])
    SC --> OA([Open to assign])
    OA --> TF([Team formed])
    TF --> SH([Scheduled])
    SC --> SH
    SH --> LV([Live])
    LV --> RD([Report drafting])
    RD --> RR([Report review])
    RR --> DL([Delivered])
    DL --> RM([Remediation])
    RM --> CL2([Closed])
    DL --> CL2
State What's happening Requested You submitted a pentest request; SecurityBoat is reviewing it. Draft Your request was approved and became an engagement. Scoping SecurityBoat is confirming scope, environment, access, and dates with you. Open to assign SecurityBoat is assembling the testing team. Team formed The testers are confirmed. Scheduled Testing dates are locked. Live Active testing is underway — verified findings appear as they are confirmed. Report drafting The testing team is writing the engagement report. Report review The report is with your team for sign-off, then SecurityBoat's final review. Delivered The final report has been issued to you. Remediation You're fixing issues; retests may follow. Closed The engagement is complete (or a request was closed before testing).

Engagement states are moved by SecurityBoat. Your part is to submit the request, provide access and context, review and approve the report, and fix and retest findings. Track requests that have not gone Live yet under My Requests.

docs.title: 2. What each client role can do
docs.text:
Action Client Admin Client TPM Client Viewer View your organisation's engagements ✅ ✅ ✅ Open engagement detail (Brief, Findings, Reports…) ✅ ✅ ✅ Submit a new pentest request ✅ ✅ ❌ Send messages in engagement Chat ✅ ✅ ❌ Approve the report or Request changes ✅ ✅ ❌ Download the final report PDF ✅ ✅ ✅ Export findings to CSV ✅ ✅ ✅ Configure Jira integration on an engagement ✅ ❌ ❌
