Why you "request" rather than "create": scope, testers, and scheduling all need SecurityBoat review. You file a request; once approved, it becomes a tracked engagement that progresses through to delivery.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Click Pentest Engagements in the main sidebar menu.

docs.title: 3. The Engagements list
docs.text:
The page is titled Pentest Engagements — "Request, scope, schedule, deliver — every PTaaS engagement on the platform."

Summary tiles: Total engagements · Live · Completed (Delivered plus Closed).

Filter pills: each pill shows a live count.

Pill What it shows All Every engagement visible to your organisation. Live Engagements where testing is actively happening. Scheduled Engagements with confirmed dates, waiting to start. Delivered Report issued; includes engagements in Remediation. Closed Completed engagements. Requested Requests you or your colleagues submitted that are still being reviewed. Archived Engagements SecurityBoat has archived. Their chat becomes read-only.

There's also a search box — Search by project ID or title…

Table columns: Engagement (title + Project ID + testing type) · Client · State · TPM (your SecurityBoat project manager) · Findings (count) · Scheduled (start → end). Click any row to open it. The list shows 10 rows per page.

New engagement button (Client Admin / Client TPM only): opens the pentest request form — see Create Engagement.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use the filter pills to find what needs attention — Live and Requested show work in flight.
  • Keep your asset inventory current before requesting a pentest.
  • Use the engagement Chat for questions during testing instead of email.
  • Review the report promptly when it reaches you — you are reminded if it waits more than 3 days.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix I can't find an engagement Check the Archived or Closed pill, or clear the search. Pre-Live requests are also listed under My Requests. No "New engagement" button You're a Client Viewer (read-only). Ask a Client Admin or Client TPM to submit the request.

Next: Create Engagement →

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text:
The Analytics tab is a read-only visual dashboard that gives you an at-a-glance view of engagement health — how many findings, how severe, how old, and how much testing is complete.

Who can view: all client roles. This tab is read-only.

docs.title: 1. KPI strip
docs.text:
Five quick-glance metrics sit across the top of the tab:

KPI What it shows Trend detail Total findings All verified findings on this engagement. "+N new this week" when new findings were added recently. Critical / High Count of the two highest-severity tiers. Breakdown shows "0 critical · N high" so you know the split. Open vs. Resolved How many findings are still open vs. already fixed. "N resolved · N open" — a rising resolved count means remediation is progressing. Methodology Percentage of the methodology checklist completed. "N/N tested" — how many checklist items have been exercised. Days in current state How long the engagement has been in its current lifecycle state. Shows the state name (e.g., "live", "report drafting") for context.

docs.title: 2. Severity breakdown
docs.text:
A horizontal bar chart showing the count of findings at each severity tier:

Tier Color What it means Critical Red Immediate risk — could lead to system compromise. High Orange Significant vulnerability requiring prompt attention. Medium Yellow Notable issue with moderate impact. Low Blue Minor issue or hardening opportunity. Informational Grey Observation without direct risk — useful context.

docs.title: 3. State funnel
docs.text:
Shows where all findings sit across the finding lifecycle — from newly submitted through to resolved. Each stage is a bar, and the funnel shape tells you:

  • Wide at the top: many new findings — testing is productive.
  • Narrow at the bottom: few resolved — remediation hasn't started yet.
  • Balanced: healthy flow from discovery through to fix.

docs.title: 4. Methodology coverage
docs.text:
Stacked progress bars per methodology category showing how much of each area has been tested. Categories are auto-resolved from the engagement's asset types (e.g., Authentication, Session Management, Input Validation for web apps).

If this panel shows 0% with the message "Checklist seeds when the engagement transitions to LIVE," testing hasn't begun yet — see the Coverage tab for details.

docs.title: 5. Open findings by age
docs.text:
Buckets open findings into age ranges to flag aging issues:

Age range What to watch for 0–7 days Fresh findings — normal. 8–30 days Starting to age — check if remediation is scheduled. 31–60 days Aging — these should have remediation plans. 60+ days Stale — escalate if no fix is in progress.

docs.title: 6. Highest-severity findings
docs.text: The top findings ranked by CVSS score, with quick links to open each one. Use this to jump directly to the most impactful issues without scrolling the full findings table.

docs.title: 7. Findings discovered (last 30 days)
docs.text:
A trend visualization showing how many findings were discovered per day over the last 30 days. This gives you testing velocity at a glance:

  • Rising trend: testers are finding more — testing may be ramping up or hitting a rich area.
  • Falling trend: testing may be winding down, or the easy findings have all been found.
  • Flat line: steady-state testing — consistent productivity.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Check Analytics before status calls — the KPI strip and age buckets answer "are we on track?" faster than scrolling individual findings.
  • Watch the Critical/High count — if it's climbing, escalate to your TPM to discuss whether testing should pause for immediate remediation.
  • Monitor findings by age — anything over 30 days without a fix plan is a conversation starter with your internal remediation team.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Methodology shows 0% The engagement hasn't reached Live yet. This is normal. No data in any chart No findings have been verified on this engagement. Charts populate as findings are submitted and verified. "Findings discovered" chart is empty No findings were created in the last 30 days. This is normal for new engagements or engagements in non-Live states.

← Previous: Findings | Next: Reports →

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: The Assets tab shows the asset under test for this engagement — its full scope contract including URLs, IP ranges, credentials, and attachments. This tab is read-only for all client roles; asset data is managed by the SecurityBoat team based on the scoping call.

docs.title: 1. Asset header
docs.text:
At the top of the tab you'll see the asset card with:

Element Description Asset name The registered asset name (e.g., "Acme Corp Web Portal"). Type badge The asset type — Web Application, API, Mobile App, Network, etc. Criticality badge Business impact rating: Low, Medium, High, or Critical. State badge Asset lifecycle state — typically "Active" for assets under test.

docs.title: 2. Overview section
docs.text:
Basic asset metadata:

Field Description Description Business context for the asset. May be empty if not provided during asset registration. Types The asset type(s). Determines which methodology checklists are auto-resolved. Criticality Business impact rating — helps the testing team prioritize effort. State Current asset state (Active, Inactive, Archived). Owner The person accountable for this asset. May show "—" if not assigned. Created / Updated Timestamps for asset record creation and last modification.

docs.title: 3. Scope section
docs.text:
Shows scope details grouped by asset type. For a Web Application asset, this typically includes:

  • URLs — the web application URLs in scope.
  • IP ranges — any IP ranges to be tested.
  • API endpoints — specific API paths if applicable.

If this section shows "No type-specific scope set," it means the asset's scope hasn't been configured yet. This is normal during Draft and early preparation stages — the SecurityBoat team finalizes scope during the scoping call.

docs.title: 4. Credentials section
docs.text:
Displays any test credentials the SecurityBoat team has on file for this asset (e.g., test accounts, VPN access, API keys). These are masked for security — you'll see placeholders rather than actual credentials.

If this section is empty, provide credentials to your TPM via the engagement Chat.

docs.title: 5. Attachments section
docs.text: Any files attached to the asset — architecture diagrams, data-flow documents, API specifications, or other reference materials the testing team may need.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Keep your asset record current — if URLs, IP ranges, or app versions have changed since the asset was registered, update the asset under Assets in the sidebar. The engagement references your asset, so keeping it current keeps the engagement scope correct.
  • Provide credentials early — test accounts, VPN access, and API keys should be shared with your TPM during the Draft stage to avoid delays when testing begins.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Scope shows "No type-specific scope set" The asset scope hasn't been configured. This is normal before the scoping call. Your TPM will set it up. Credentials section is empty No credentials have been provided for this asset. Share them with your TPM via Chat. Asset details look wrong The asset record may be outdated. Update it under Assets in the sidebar, then notify your TPM.

← Previous: Brief | Next: Team →

docs.title: Brief
docs.text: The Brief tab is the default landing view when you open an engagement. It gives you a complete snapshot of scope, schedule, and team in a single scroll — no clicking through other tabs required.

docs.title: 1. Layout
docs.text:
The Brief tab uses a two-column layout:

Column Content Left (main) Overview card, Description, Rules of engagement (In-scope / Out-of-scope) Right (sidebar) Schedule card, Testing team card, State history timeline

docs.title: 2. Overview card (left column)
docs.text:
The top section shows four metric chips summarizing the engagement's configuration:

Chip Possible values What it tells you Engagement types Web Application, API/Web Services, Mobile, Network Infrastructure, Cloud, Hardware, IoT, Other What kind of system is being tested. An engagement can have multiple types. Testing approach Black box, Grey box, White box How much knowledge the testers have about the system internals. Environment Production, UAT, Staging, QA, Development Where the testing is being conducted. Source-code access Granted, Not granted Whether the testing team has access to the application source code.

Below the chips is the Description you provided when submitting the request. If it shows "No description added," this means the request was submitted with minimal context — not necessarily a problem, but richer descriptions reduce back-and-forth during scoping.

docs.title: 3. Rules of engagement card (left column)
docs.text:
Defines what the testing team is authorized to test:

  • In-scope — systems, URLs, IP ranges, and paths the testers can probe. If this shows "No in-scope added," the scope is still being finalized by the SecurityBoat team.
  • Out-of-scope — explicitly excluded targets (e.g., third-party integrations, production data endpoints). Review this to confirm it matches your expectations.

The in-scope and out-of-scope notes you enter in the request form are carried over here. SecurityBoat may refine them during scoping.

If scope looks wrong: use the engagement Chat to flag it to your TPM before testing begins. Changes after Live testing has started may require a scope amendment.

docs.title: 4. Schedule card (right column)
docs.text:
Shows the engagement timeline at a glance:

Field Description Window progress A percentage bar indicating how far through the scheduled testing window you currently are. Scheduled start / end The planned testing window dates. Actual start / end When testing actually began and ended. Shows "—" if testing hasn't started yet. Testing effort (hrs) Budgeted testing hours for this engagement.

docs.title: 5. Testing team card (right column)
docs.text:
A compact roster of who's working your engagement:

  • Lead Researcher count + list (name, email)
  • Researcher count + list

The TPM (your primary contact) is not always listed here — you'll find them on the Team tab and in engagement communications.

docs.title: 6. State history card (right column)
docs.text:
A vertical timeline of every state transition the engagement has gone through. Each entry shows when the engagement moved from one state to the next. For new engagements that haven't transitioned yet, this shows "No transitions yet."

The full lifecycle stepper (visible in the page header) shows all 12 possible states: Requested → Draft → Scoping → Open to assign → Team formed → Scheduled → Live → Report drafting → Report review → Delivered → Remediation → Closed.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Start here every time — the Brief tab answers "what are we testing, who's doing it, and where are we in the timeline" in one view.
  • Check rules of engagement early — if scope is incorrect, flag it in Chat before the engagement goes Live.
  • Watch the window progress bar — if you're past 80% and haven't seen findings yet, check with your TPM.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Description says "No description added" The request was submitted with minimal context. You can provide additional details via Chat. In-scope / Out-of-scope is empty Scope hasn't been finalized yet. This is normal during Draft and early preparation stages. State history is empty The engagement hasn't transitioned states yet — normal for newly created engagements. Schedule shows "—" for actual dates Testing hasn't started yet. Actual start/end populate once testing begins.

← Previous: Engagement Detail | Next: Assets →

docs.title: Chat
docs.text: The Chat tab is a dedicated message thread scoped to this engagement — the fastest way to ask a question, provide credentials, or clarify scope without leaving the platform. Messages stay permanently attached to the engagement record.

docs.title: 1. Who can do what
docs.text:
Action Client Admin Client TPM Client Viewer Read messages ✅ ✅ ✅ Send messages ✅ ✅ ❌ Choose visibility (Everyone / Client only) ✅ ✅ —

Client Viewers can read the full chat history but cannot send messages. If you need to communicate something to the team, ask a Client Admin or TPM in your organization.

docs.title: 2. Message visibility
docs.text:
When sending a message, use the Visible to dropdown to control who sees it:

Visibility Who can read it Everyone Everyone in this chat — the testers, your TPM and SecurityBoat staff, and your organisation's members. Use this for general questions, scope clarifications, and status updates. Client only Your organisation's members plus SecurityBoat staff (SB Admin, CSM, TPM). The testers (researchers) cannot see it. Use this for discussions with SecurityBoat that the testers don't need to see.

Each message shows a badge with its audience. You always see your own messages.

docs.title: Mentioning people
docs.text: Type @ in the composer to mention someone on the engagement. Only people who can read the message (based on the audience you chose) can be mentioned, and they receive a notification.

docs.title: 3. Rich text editor
docs.text:
The chat composer supports both Rich text and Markdown modes — toggle between them with the tabs above the input area.

Rich text mode includes a formatting toolbar:

  • Bold (⌘B), Italic (⌘I), Strikethrough
  • Inline code
  • Clear formatting
  • Insert link
  • Undo / Redo

Markdown mode supports standard syntax:

  • **bold** · *italic* · `code`
  • ``` code block ``` — paste raw HTTP/JSON and it auto-formats as a code block
  • # heading · - list · > quote
  • ⌘K to insert a link

A Preview tab lets you review your message formatting before sending.

docs.title: 4. Empty state
docs.text: If no messages have been sent yet, the tab shows "No messages yet. Start the conversation." and "0 of 0 messages visible." This is normal for newly created engagements — start the conversation whenever you have something to communicate.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Use Chat instead of email — messages stay attached to the engagement record and are visible to anyone on the team who needs context later.
  • Provide credentials in Chat — test accounts, VPN access, or API keys shared here are visible to the testing team immediately.
  • Be specific — instead of "can you check something?", say "the login page at /auth returns a 500 error with test account user@test.com."
  • Use Client only for discussions with SecurityBoat that the testers don't need to see. Remember that SecurityBoat staff can read Client only messages.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Can't send messages You're a Client Viewer (read-only). Ask a Client Admin or TPM in your organization to send on your behalf. Message I sent isn't visible to the testers You selected Client only. Resend with Everyone if the testers need to see it. I can't @mention someone They can't read a message with the audience you selected. Chat shows "0 of 0 messages" No messages have been sent yet. This is normal for new engagements. Formatting isn't applying Switch to Preview tab to check how your message will render, or toggle to Rich text mode for WYSIWYG formatting.

← Previous: Reports | Next: Integrations →

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
The Coverage tab shows the methodology checklist — the set of test items being exercised on your engagement, grouped by security category. This gives you visibility into testing progress without needing to wait for the final report.

Who can view: all client roles. This tab is read-only — status updates are managed by the testing team.

docs.title: 1. How the checklist works
docs.text:
When an engagement transitions to Live, a methodology checklist is automatically seeded based on the engagement's asset types. For example, a Web Application asset triggers web-focused test items (Authentication, Session Management, Input Validation, etc.).

Each checklist item has a status:

Status Meaning Not started Testing hasn't begun on this item yet. In progress A tester is actively working on this item. Tested — no finding The item was tested and no vulnerability was found. Tested — finding raised Testing uncovered an issue — a finding was submitted. Not applicable The item doesn't apply to this engagement's scope.

Statuses update in real time as testers work through the checklist.

docs.title: 2. Empty state
docs.text:
If the Coverage tab shows a message like:

"Checklist seeds when the engagement transitions to LIVE. Methodology is auto-resolved from the engagement's asset types — make sure at least one matching template exists in Admin → Methodology."

This means one of two things:

  1. The engagement hasn't reached Live yet. The checklist populates when active testing begins. This is normal for Draft, Scheduled, and pre-Live states.
  2. No methodology template matches the asset type. A SecurityBoat admin needs to create a methodology template for this asset type under Admin → Methodology.

In either case, no action is needed from you — the checklist will populate automatically once the conditions are met.

docs.title: 3. Reading the coverage progress
docs.text:
The methodology completion percentage (also visible on the Analytics tab) tells you how much of the planned testing has been executed. Use this alongside the findings count to gauge testing velocity:

  • Low coverage + few findings: testing is still ramping up — early days.
  • High coverage + few findings: thorough testing, clean results — good sign.
  • High coverage + many findings: testing is productive — expect the report to reflect this.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Don't panic if coverage is 0% — the checklist seeds when testing goes Live. If the engagement is still in Draft or Scheduled, this is expected.
  • Use coverage alongside Analytics — the methodology completion % tells you "how much has been tested," while Analytics tells you "what was found."
  • Check coverage before status calls — it's a fast way to answer "how far along is the testing?"

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Coverage tab is empty / shows seeding message The engagement hasn't reached Live yet, or no methodology template exists for the asset type. The SecurityBoat team handles this — no action needed from you. Coverage percentage seems stuck Testers may be working on complex items that take longer. Check the Analytics tab for findings-created-per-day to confirm activity. All items show "Not applicable" The methodology template may not match the engagement's asset types. Flag this to your TPM via Chat.

← Previous: Team | Next: Findings →

docs.title: Engagement Detail
docs.text: Opening an engagement from the list takes you to its detail page — the central workspace for tracking your pentest from approval through to final report delivery. The page has a header (identity, state, and key metrics) followed by a row of nine tabs.

docs.title: 1. The header
docs.text: Element What it shows Project ID The engagement's permanent reference code (e.g., PT-ACME-001). Quote this when contacting your SecurityBoat team. State badge The current lifecycle state, color-coded. States like "Live" and "Report review" include a subtle pulse animation indicating active progress. Title The engagement name you gave it when submitting the request. Client badge Your organization's avatar and name — confirms which client account the engagement belongs to. Lifecycle stepper A visual 12-step path showing how far the engagement has progressed: Requested → Draft → Scoping → Open to assign → Team formed → Scheduled → Live → Report drafting → Report review → Delivered → Remediation → Closed. Completed steps are checked, the current step glows, future steps are hollow. KPI tiles Four quick-glance metrics: Effort (hours) · Issues found · Team size · Days remaining. The "Days remaining" tile turns amber inside 7 days and red inside 2 — a heads-up that the testing window is closing.

docs.title: 2. The tabs
docs.text:
Nine tabs give you different perspectives on the engagement. Click any tab name below for a dedicated guide with screenshots and details:

Tab What it shows Guide Brief Scope overview, testing approach, schedule, rules of engagement, testing team, and state history. Brief → Assets The asset under test and its full scope contract (URLs, IP ranges, credentials, attachments). Read-only. Assets → Team The SecurityBoat team assigned to your engagement — lead researcher, researchers, and their roles. Team → Coverage The methodology checklist showing what's been tested, grouped by security category. Coverage → Findings All verified findings for this engagement — filter by severity, state, and asset type, and export to CSV with the columns you choose. Findings → Analytics Visual dashboards — severity breakdown, state funnel, methodology coverage, findings by age, and discovery trend. Analytics → Reports The engagement report — review it, Approve report or Request changes, and download the PDF once SecurityBoat marks it Final. Reports → Chat Direct messaging with the engagement team via rich-text or Markdown editor with visibility controls. Chat → Integrations Jira project mapping to push findings to your issue tracker. Client Admin only. Integrations →

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Start on the Brief tab — it's the fastest way to re-orient on scope, schedule, and recent progress before diving into Findings or Reports.
  • Check Analytics before status calls — the KPI strip and age buckets answer "are we on track?" faster than scrolling individual findings.
  • Use Chat proactively — if you have questions about a finding or need to provide updated credentials, send it in Chat so the team sees it immediately.
  • Review the report when it reaches you — Client Admin or Client TPM approves it (or requests changes) before SecurityBoat's final review.
  • Wait for "Final" before circulating the report — the Download PDF button only activates once SecurityBoat marks the report Final.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Coverage tab is empty The engagement hasn't reached the Live testing state yet. It will populate once testing begins. Download PDF is greyed out The report hasn't been marked as Final yet. Even after you approve it, SecurityBoat completes a final review before the download unlocks. Integrations tab is missing Only Client Admin can manage Jira mappings. Ask your admin if you need this configured. Can't send messages in Chat You're a Client Viewer (read-only). Ask a Client Admin or TPM if you need to communicate something to the team.

← Previous: Create Engagement | Next: Brief →

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
The Findings tab lists every verified finding raised on this engagement — the same data you'd see in the platform-wide Findings module, pre-filtered to this engagement.

Who can view: all client roles. Clients cannot create or edit findings; Client Admin and Client TPM move findings through remediation from the finding's detail page.

docs.title: 1. Findings table
docs.text: Column Description ID The finding's reference code. Quote it when discussing a finding. Title A short description. Click to open the full finding. Asset The asset the finding was discovered on, or "—". Severity Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Informational. State Verified, Fix in progress, Ready for retest, Accepted risk, or Resolved. Created When the finding was submitted.

docs.title: 2. Filters
docs.text: Filter Use Severity Show only Critical, High, etc. State Show only findings in one state — for example everything awaiting retest. Asset type Narrow multi-asset engagements to one asset type.

docs.title: 3. Export CSV
docs.text: Click Export CSV to open the Export findings to CSV dialog. Choose which states to include and tick the columns you want. The default columns are Finding ID, Title, Severity, State, Vulnerability type, CVSS score, CWE ID, CVE ID, Endpoint URL, Description, Impact, Remediation, Submitter, and Created at. See Exporting findings to CSV for the full list of fields.

docs.title: 4. Finding detail and remediation
docs.text:
Click any finding row to open its detail page: description, evidence, CVSS score, remediation guidance, comments, and the state timeline.

flowchart LR
    V([Verified]) --> F([Fix in progress]) --> R([Ready for retest]) --> D([Resolved])
    R -->|retest failed| F

From the State actions panel, Client Admin or Client TPM can Acknowledge and start fixing and then Submit fix for retest. The testing team confirms the fix. A Client Admin can also Accept risk formally. See the Findings guide for the full lifecycle.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Filter by severity — handle Critical and High first.
  • Filter by state = Ready for retest to see what is waiting on the testers.
  • Export before meetings with only the columns your audience needs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Findings tab shows 0 results Testing may not have started, or nothing has been verified yet. Check the Coverage tab. Expected finding isn't visible Pentest findings appear only after the testing team verifies them. CSV export doesn't include a finding Check the state selection in the export dialog and your active filters.

← Previous: Coverage | Next: Analytics →

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
The Integrations tab lets you connect this engagement to a Jira project so findings can be automatically pushed into your existing issue tracker.

Who can view and configure: Client Admin only. Client TPM and Client Viewer cannot see or manage this tab.

docs.title: 1. Jira connection status
docs.text:
The tab shows one of two states:

State What you see Not connected "Jira not connected" with a prompt to connect your Jira account in Settings → Integrations. Connected A dropdown to select a Jira project for this engagement, plus sync status.

docs.title: 2. Setting up Jira (first time)
docs.text:
If Jira isn't connected yet:

  1. Go to Settings → Integrations in the sidebar (or click the link in the prompt).
  2. Follow the Jira connection flow to authorize your Jira instance.
  3. Return to this engagement's Integrations tab.
  4. Select a Jira project from the dropdown.
  5. New findings can now be exported as Jira issues directly from the platform.

docs.title: 3. After connecting
docs.text:
Once a Jira project is mapped to this engagement:

  • Export findings: each finding gets an "Export to Jira" action that creates a linked Jira issue.
  • Bi-directional sync: updates to the finding in Tri-Netra (state changes, comments) can be configured to sync to the Jira issue.
  • One project per engagement: you map a single Jira project per engagement. For multi-project workflows, coordinate with your TPM.

docs.title: 4. If the tab is missing
docs.text: Only Client Admin can see and manage the Integrations tab. If you're a Client TPM or Viewer and need Jira integration configured, ask your organization's Client Admin to set it up.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Connect Jira before testing begins — findings start appearing as soon as testing goes Live. Having the integration ready means you can push them to your team's backlog immediately.
  • Use a dedicated Jira project — mapping each engagement to its own Jira project keeps remediation tracking clean and prevents cross-engagement confusion.
  • Verify the sync direction — confirm with your TPM whether you want one-way export (Tri-Netra → Jira) or bi-directional sync.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Integrations tab is missing entirely Only Client Admin can manage Jira mappings. Ask your admin to configure it. "Jira not connected" message Your organization hasn't connected a Jira instance yet. Go to Settings → Integrations to set it up. Jira project dropdown is empty Your Jira instance is connected but no projects are visible. Check Jira permissions — your account needs project access. Exported finding doesn't appear in Jira The sync may have a delay, or the finding's state may not trigger an export. Check with your TPM if automatic sync is configured.

← Previous: Chat | Next: My Requests →

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: The Reports tab is where you review and receive the engagement's deliverable — the penetration test report. Your team signs the report off first, then SecurityBoat completes a final review and releases it for download.

docs.title: 1. The report approval lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    D([Draft]) -->|testing team submits| IR([In review])
    IR -->|you: Approve report| CA([Client Approved])
    IR -->|you: Request changes| RJ([Rejected])
    RJ -->|revised and resubmitted| IR
    CA -->|SecurityBoat: Mark Final| F([✓ Final])
    CA -->|SecurityBoat sends back| RJ
    F -->|after retest| PR([✓ Post-Retest Final])
Status What it means for you Draft The testing team is writing the report. You can preview the current version. In review The report is ready for your review. Client Admin or Client TPM approves it or requests changes. Rejected Changes were requested. The testing team revises and resubmits it. Client Approved You approved the report. SecurityBoat is completing its final review. ✓ Final The report is released — you can now download the PDF. ✓ Post-Retest Final The report was re-issued after a retest confirmed your fixes. Also downloadable.

A coloured badge at the top of the Reports tab always shows the current status, and a banner tells you what happens next.

docs.title: 2. What you can do
docs.text: Action Client Admin Client TPM Client Viewer Preview the report ✅ ✅ ✅ Approve report (while In review) ✅ ✅ ❌ Request changes (while In review) ✅ ✅ ❌ Download the PDF ✅ (Final / Post-Retest Final) ✅ (Final / Post-Retest Final) ✅ (Final / Post-Retest Final)

docs.title: 3. Reviewing the report (Client Admin / Client TPM)
docs.text:
When the report reaches In review, you are notified and the tab shows:

⏳ Ready for your review — sent (time). Approve the report or request changes.

  1. Read the inline preview — executive summary, scope, findings, and recommendations.
  2. Choose one:
    • Approve report — records your approval and sends the report for SecurityBoat's final review. The download unlocks once that review is complete.
    • Request changes — sends the report back to the testing team with your feedback.
  3. In the dialog, enter a Description of Changes (at least 5 characters) — your approval note or the changes you want. It is recorded in the report's document-control history.

After you approve, the tab reads:

✓ You approved this report. SecurityBoat is completing the final review — the download will unlock once that is done.

If a report waits for review for more than 3 days, your team and your TPM receive a reminder.

docs.title: 4. Downloading the final PDF
docs.text:
Once the report reaches ✓ Final or ✓ Post-Retest Final, the tab reads "✓ Final (time) — the report is ready to download."

  1. Open the Reports tab.
  2. Click Download PDF.

Report title: every report has a title, and the scheduled month and year are added to it automatically (for example "— Oct — 2026").

Post-Retest Final: after you remediate findings and they are retested, SecurityBoat may re-issue the report as Post-Retest Final. It confirms which findings were resolved and is the authoritative post-remediation record.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Review promptly — testing is not complete for you until the report is signed off.
  • Request changes with specifics — name the section and what is wrong (scope URL, contact name, severity wording).
  • Wait for the Final badge before sharing the report externally.
  • Keep both versions if a Post-Retest Final is issued.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No Approve / Request changes buttons The report isn't In review, or you are Client Viewer. Download PDF is greyed out after I approved SecurityBoat's final review is still pending. The download unlocks at Final. Report preview is empty The testing team hasn't started the narrative yet. This is normal during Live testing.

← Previous: Analytics | Next: Chat →

docs.title: Team
docs.text: The Team tab shows you who SecurityBoat has assigned to work on your engagement. As a client user, this tab is read-only — you can see the roster but team composition is managed by SecurityBoat.

docs.title: 1. Understanding the team roles
docs.text:
Every engagement is staffed with a combination of the following roles:

Role What they do for you TPM (Technical Project Manager) Your primary point of contact at SecurityBoat. They coordinate the engagement, review the report, and answer your questions. Lead Researcher Runs the hands-on testing effort and authors the engagement report. Researcher(s) Test against the scope and methodology checklist, and submit findings. An engagement may have several researchers working in parallel.

docs.title: 2. What you see
docs.text:
Each team member's entry shows:

  • Avatar and name — who they are.
  • Role badge — their function on this engagement (TPM, Lead researcher, or Researcher).
  • Email — in case you need to reference them outside the platform.

If a team member was removed mid-engagement (e.g. replaced by another researcher), they'll appear with a muted "removed" label. Their prior contributions (findings, messages) remain attributed to them.

docs.title: 3. When the team is empty
docs.text: If no team has been assigned yet, you'll see a placeholder message. This is normal for engagements that are still in the Draft or internal preparation stages. Once SecurityBoat completes team assembly, the roster populates automatically — no action needed from you.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Know your TPM by name — they're the person to reach out to (via Chat or email) for any questions about timeline, scope, or report status.
  • Check the team size before your engagement goes Live — if you expected a larger team (e.g. for a complex multi-app engagement), raise it with your TPM early during the Draft stage.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Team tab shows "No team assigned yet" The engagement is still in preparation. The team will appear once SecurityBoat finishes assembling it. A team member I expected isn't listed They may not have been assigned to this specific engagement. Reach out to your TPM in Chat to confirm the roster.

← Previous: Assets | Next: Coverage →

docs.title: Security Researcher — Getting Started
docs.text:
Version 4.2 — August 2026 · Production guide for live researchers · en-GB

Welcome to the Security Researcher guide. As a researcher on Tri-Netra, you participate in penetration testing engagements and bug bounty programs to discover, document, and report security vulnerabilities.

docs.title: 1. Role & Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Testing & Finding Submission: Test assigned assets according to engagement scope, document reproducible PoCs, score vulnerabilities using CVSS v4.0, and submit findings for TPM verification.
  • Coverage Tracking: Log methodology progress using the engagement coverage checklist.
  • Retesting: Verify client remediations when assigned retest tasks.
  • Report Drafting (Lead Researchers): Draft report narratives and executive summaries for review by the TPM.

docs.title: Submitting a Finding
docs.text:
1. Open your assigned engagement from Pentest Engagements.
  2. Click the Findings tab and select Submit finding.
  3. Fill in the title, CVSS v4.0 vector, vulnerability type, affected endpoint, detailed description, business impact, remediation advice, and PoC evidence.
  4. Save as Draft to continue editing, or click Submit to send to the TPM review queue.

docs.title: Managing Payouts
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Payouts to set up bank details and payout preferences.
  2. Track earnings from verified findings and engagement fees in Payouts.

docs.title: 3. Chapter Index
docs.text:
For complete step-by-step instructions, see the chapters below:

  1. Introduction — Role overview and scope rules
  2. Logging In — Single Sign-On (SSO), MFA, and session management
  3. Dashboard — Work hub, active engagements, open findings, and pay
  4. Opportunities — Marketplace bidding and application flows
  5. Invites — Direct invitations and response workflows
  6. Engagements — Brief, assets, coverage checklists, team chat, and reports
  7. Findings — The 7-card finding submission form and CVSS v4.0 calculator
  8. Payouts — Earnings, payout statuses, eligibility countdowns, and invoice downloads
  9. Identity Verification — Passkey/ID document and liveness check flow
  10. Bug Bounty — Continuous testing programs and VDP participation
  11. Hacktivity — Public feed of disclosed vulnerability reports
  12. Disclosure Requests — Submit and track public disclosure requests
  13. AI Assistant (Ish) — Data-aware chat powered by Ish scoped to researcher data
  14. Feedback — Submit platform bug reports and feature requests
  15. Settings — Account, bank details, MFA, and notifications

Next: Introduction →

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text: Tri-Netra is the platform through which SecurityBoat engages security researchers to test its customers' systems. This guide is for the Researcher (and Lead Researcher) — the people who do the actual security testing: joining engagements, hunting vulnerabilities, and authoring findings.

docs.title: Your role in one line
docs.text:
A Researcher works on the engagements they've been added to and the bug-bounty programs they participate in. You see your opportunities and invites, the engagements you're seated on, the findings you author, your payouts, and your identity verification — all scoped to you. You never see another org's private data or another researcher's pay.

A Lead Researcher does everything a researcher does, plus coordinates the testing team on an engagement (a slightly richer dashboard and team view).

docs.title: What you can do on Tri-Netra (Researcher modules)
docs.text: Module What it does Your access Dashboard Your testing snapshot — active engagements, your open findings, your pay. View Opportunities Open engagement opportunities you can express interest in. View / apply Invites Direct invitations to join specific engagements. Accept / decline Engagements The engagements you're seated on — scope, team, timeline. View / work Findings Vulnerabilities on your engagements. View / author My Findings The findings you personally authored, across engagements. View / manage Payouts Your earnings and payout history (your scope only). View Identity Verification Complete background/identity verification to unlock work. Complete Bug Bounty Programs you participate in — submit and track reports. View / submit AI Assistant (Ish) Ask questions about your engagements and findings powered by Ish. Use Notifications Your alerts and updates. View Settings Your account, MFA, and notification preferences. Manage own

docs.title: How to use this guide
docs.text:
Each chapter covers one module in depth — its purpose, how to reach it, every control on the page, the end-to-end flow, and exactly what your role can and can't do. Start with Login, then your Dashboard.

← Previous: Getting Started | Next: Login →

docs.title: 1. How you get access
docs.text:
Access to Tri-Netra is invite-only. Here's how you get onboarded as a researcher:

  1. Apply. Click Apply as a researcher on the sign-in screen and submit your application.
  2. Get approved. SecurityBoat reviews your application.
  3. Receive your invitation. Once approved, you get an invitation email with a setup link.
  4. Set up your account. Follow the link to create your password and set up MFA.

After setup, you sign in whenever you're ready to work.

docs.title: 2. The sign-in screen
docs.text:
Open your Tri-Netra URL. You'll see the sign-in screen with:

  • Continue with SSO — the main sign-in button. Click this every time you sign in.
  • Apply as a researcher — for new researchers who haven't applied yet.
  • Lost access to your authenticator app? Reset MFA → — self-service link to recover your account if you lose your authenticator app.
  • Contact sales — for prospective customers (not relevant to researchers).

docs.title: 3. Signing in — what you actually do
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Click Continue with SSO] --> B[Enter your email + password]
    B --> C[Enter MFA code if prompted]
    C --> D[Dashboard — you're in]
  1. Click "Continue with SSO". Your browser opens the sign-in page.
  2. Enter your email and password. These are the credentials you set up when you accepted your invitation.
  3. Enter your MFA code if prompted (from your authenticator app).
  4. You land on your Dashboard. Everything is scoped to your engagements, findings, and payouts.

docs.title: 4. First-time setup (from an invitation)
docs.text:
1. Open the invitation email and click the link inside.
  2. Set your password — pick something strong and unique.
  3. Set up MFA if prompted — scan the QR code with your authenticator app.
  4. After setup, sign in anytime by clicking Continue with SSO on the sign-in screen.

Before you can work on paid engagements, you'll usually need to complete Identity Verification — see that chapter.

docs.title: 5. Managing MFA
docs.text:
• Set up or change MFA: go to Settings → MFA Setup once signed in.
  • Lost your authenticator? Click Reset MFA on the sign-in page, enter your registered email address, and click the link sent to your email (valid for 15 minutes) to reset your factors.

docs.title: 6. Signing out
docs.text: Click your avatar (top-right) → Sign out. Always sign out on shared or public devices.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Set up MFA — it's your strongest protection against account takeover.
  • Never share your login — accounts are per-person and all activity is audited.
  • Complete identity verification early — you can't be seated on paid engagements without it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom What to do "You're not invited" or access denied Your application may still be under review, or you haven't accepted your invitation yet. Can't sign in with your password Use the password reset option on the sign-in page. Lost MFA device Click Reset MFA on the sign-in screen and use the self-service email recovery link, or contact support if you need assistance. Signed out unexpectedly Sessions expire after inactivity for security. Sign in again — it takes 30 seconds.

← Previous: Introduction | Next: Dashboard →

docs.title: 1. What the Dashboard is for
docs.text:
The Researcher Dashboard is your personal work hub. It shows only what's yours — the engagements you're on, the findings you've authored, the programs you work on, and your earnings — so you can jump straight into testing. It answers:

  • What am I working on right now? (live engagements)
  • What findings do I still own? (my open findings)
  • How am I doing? (performance, disclosed findings, earnings)

Every card links into the module where you act.

docs.title: 2. How to reach it
docs.text:
• Loads automatically after login.
  • Click Dashboard at the top of the left sidebar, or the Tri-Netra logo.

docs.title: a. Greeting banner
docs.text: Your first name and role, with the subtitle "Your engagements, findings and security research activity."

docs.title: b. Identity Verification card (conditional)
docs.text: If SecurityBoat has requested identity verification from you, a card appears prompting you to complete it. See the Identity Verification chapter.

docs.title: c. KPI tiles
docs.text: Tile Meaning Live engagements Engagements you're on that are being tested now. My open findings Findings you authored that are not yet resolved. Disclosed findings Your findings published on Hacktivity. Total earnings (own scope) Your total earnings. This is your figure only.

docs.title: d. Action Needed, Quick status, and My Performance
docs.text:
• Action Needed — items waiting on you.
  • Quick status — shortcuts to pre-filtered Findings pages: Verified findings, Resolved findings, BB findings, PTaaS findings.
  • My Performance — your activity, including Findings submitted over the last 6 months.

docs.title: e. Recent work
docs.text:
• Recent Engagements and Recent BB Programs side by side.
  • Recent Findings (tabs All, BB, PTaaS) and Recommended Programs side by side.

Sections for a module you don't have access to (PTaaS or Bug Bounty) are hidden.

docs.title: 4. Lead Researcher differences
docs.text: A Lead Researcher sees "Engagements you're leading + the findings backlog you authored." with the tiles Engagements I lead and My open findings.

docs.title: 5. How to use it day to day
docs.text:
1. Complete the verification card if it's shown.
  2. Open Live engagements to continue testing.
  3. Use Quick status to jump to verified or resolved findings.
  4. Check Recommended Programs for new Bug Bounty work.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No engagements shown You aren't on any engagement yet — check Opportunities and Invites. Earnings show zero You have no recorded earnings yet. Verification card won't go away Your verification isn't complete — open it and finish the steps.

← Previous: Login | Next: Opportunities →

docs.title: 1. What Opportunities is
docs.text:
Opportunities is the researcher marketplace: a feed of open pentest engagements you can bid on. SecurityBoat posts sanitised scope summaries here when an engagement opens for bids. You browse, find work that fits your skills, and apply — as a Researcher or a Lead Researcher.

Privacy by design: the customer's identity is not shown in the marketplace. You see the project ID (e.g. SB-PTEST-ACM-05), scope summary, pentest type, duration, and payout — the client name is revealed only after your bid is accepted. This protects the client and keeps bidding merit-based.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Click Opportunities in the sidebar. (Researcher / Lead Researcher only.)

docs.title: 2. Browsing open engagements
docs.text:
Each opportunity is a collapsible card displaying its Project ID badge (e.g. SB-PTEST-ACM-05) and Title. Click any card to expand its detail panel:

Field Description / Value Project ID Unique uppercase project identifier code. Pentest Type The target surface types (e.g., Web Application, API & Web Services, Mobile, Network). Testing Type Black-box / Grey-box / White-box testing approach. Pentest Duration Calculated automatically from scheduled start and end dates (e.g., "2 weeks", "1 day"), or testing hours. Testing Hours Total budgeted testing hours (e.g., 40h). Fixed Payout Fixed compensation amount + currency (e.g., INR 45,000), or "Contact for details". Tags Visual pills indicating Source access vs Black-box only, and scheduled execution date range (YYYY-MM-DD → YYYY-MM-DD).

docs.title: 3. Applying (placing a bid)
docs.text:
At the bottom of an expanded opportunity card:

Button / State Action / Meaning Apply as Researcher Submits your bid to join the engagement team as a security researcher. Apply as Lead Researcher Submits your bid to lead the engagement, coordinate testing, and author the report narrative. ✓ You have already applied for this opportunity Confirms your bid has been recorded; disables further submissions on this item.

After applying, your application status persists. If your bid is accepted by the SecurityBoat CSM/TPM, the engagement will appear in your Pentest Engagements view with full client identity and asset access unlocked.

Researcher vs Lead Researcher: a Lead Researcher owns the drafting of the report narrative on the engagement's Reports tab. Only apply as Lead if you are prepared to lead team coordination and report authoring.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Bid to your strengths — select opportunities that align with your verified skills and asset expertise.
  • Review duration & hours — ensure your schedule accommodates the required testing window.
  • Check payout currency — payouts are processed in the displayed currency (e.g., INR / USD).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix "No open engagements right now" No active opportunities are currently accepting bids. Check back regularly or reach out to your CSM. Client identity hidden Intentional privacy protection; organization name is revealed upon bid acceptance. Already applied banner You have already submitted a bid for this engagement. Track status under Invites or Engagements.

← Previous: Dashboard | Next: Invites →

docs.title: 1. What Invites are
docs.text:
Invites are direct invitations to join a private Bug Bounty / VDP program or a pentest engagement — as opposed to the open Opportunities marketplace where you apply. If someone wants you specifically, it shows up here.

The page is titled Program & Engagement Invites — "View and manage your invitations to bug bounty programs and pentest engagements."

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Click Invites in the sidebar (Researcher / Lead Researcher only). Invitation notifications also open this page.

docs.title: 2. The Invites list
docs.text:
Filters:

  • Status: All, Pending, Accepted, Rejected
  • Source: All Sources, Bug Bounty, Pentest

Each invite shows:

Field Meaning Name The program or engagement you are invited to. Source badge BB (Bug Bounty / VDP) or PTaaS (pentest engagement). Organisation The organisation the program or engagement belongs to. Invited by & date Who invited you — a SecurityBoat team member, or a client admin for a client-run private program — and when. Shown for pentest invites too. Status Pending (amber; awaiting your response), Accepted (green), or Rejected (red).

docs.title: 3. Responding to invitations
docs.text:
For Pending Bug Bounty invitations you get two actions:

  • Accept — opens the Accept Invite dialog, where you can add an optional note for the program manager. Once accepted, the program opens for you.
  • Reject — opens the Reject Invite dialog, where you can give an optional reason (e.g. "Schedule conflict").

Pentest invites are informational. Your place on a pentest team is confirmed by SecurityBoat (usually through an application on Opportunities), so pentest rows have no Accept / Reject buttons.

flowchart LR
    I[Invitation received] --> P([Pending])
    P -->|Accept| A([Accepted])
    P -->|Reject| R([Rejected])
    A --> O[Program or engagement opens for you]

If you are later removed from a private program, you lose access to it.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Respond promptly — program teams rely on your confirmation.
  • Add a short note when rejecting — it helps the team keep you in mind for future work.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix "No invites found" No invites match the selected filters. Switch both filters to All. I accepted but can't see the program The program may not be Active yet, or you were removed later. Check the program's status in BB Program. No Accept / Reject on a pentest invite Expected — pentest team membership is managed by SecurityBoat.

← Previous: Opportunities | Next: Engagements →

docs.title: 1. Findings are your deliverable
docs.text:
A finding is a documented vulnerability you discover. Findings are your primary deliverable and what drives rewards and payouts. You author them inside a pentest engagement or a Bug Bounty program, provide clear proof-of-concept evidence, and submit them for triage.

Note: There is no "New finding" button on the Findings page. Findings are created from the engagement's or program's Findings tab, so each one is automatically linked to the right scope.

docs.title: 2. What a researcher can do
docs.text: Action Researcher Lead Researcher Submit findings on your engagements and on Active Bug Bounty programs ✅ ✅ See your own Draft findings ✅ ✅ (plus drafts on engagements you lead) Edit your own pentest findings (until Resolved) ✅ ✅ (any finding on engagements you lead) Edit a Bug Bounty report after you submit it ❌ ❌ Verify pentest findings on engagements you lead ❌ ✅ Confirm a pentest fix after retest ✅ (your own findings) ✅ Change Bug Bounty triage states ❌ ❌

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Click Findings in the main sidebar to browse findings across your engagements and programs. To see one engagement or program, use its Findings tab.

docs.title: 3. Your findings list
docs.text:
Control / Column Meaning Summary counts Findings, Critical, High, Open, Resolved. Search Search by title or finding ID… Filters All states (including Draft), All severity, All sources — saved in the page address. ID, Title, Severity, State, Source, Submitted One row per finding. Click to open it. Export CSV Choose the columns and download the findings you can see.

When you filter by New, a popover explains the difference: for pentests the state is shown as Triaging; for Bug Bounty and VDP it is shown as New (awaiting initial review).

docs.title: 4. Submitting a finding
docs.text: Click Submit finding on the engagement's or program's Findings tab. A drawer opens with the finding form.

docs.title: Title & classification
docs.text:
• Title — short, specific summary (up to 255 characters). Required.
  • Asset type — Web Application, API & Web Services, Mobile iOS / Android, Cloud, Network, Source Code, AI/LLM, and more. It decides whether endpoint fields are required.
  • Vulnerability type (OWASP) — pick the OWASP category, or Other and describe it. Required.
  • VRT category (Bugcrowd taxonomy) — required. Selecting one pre-fills the CWE.
  • CWE — format CWE-79. Required.
  • CVE (optional) and MITRE ATT&CK (optional).

docs.title: Severity & CVSS v4.0
docs.text: • Complete all 11 CVSS v4.0 metrics. Severity is derived from the score and cannot be set by hand.

docs.title: Writeup
docs.text: • Background, Description, Steps to reproduce, Impact, Remediation — each at least 20 characters. Drag screenshots or PoC files into the editor.

docs.title: CIA triad impact
docs.text: • Impact level and a description (at least 10 characters) for Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.

docs.title: OWASP risk rating
docs.text: • Likelihood (0-9) and Impact (0-9) — required. They place the finding on the report's risk heat matrix.

docs.title: References
docs.text: • At least one reference URL (vendor advisory, OWASP page, etc.). Required.

docs.title: Endpoint and evidence
docs.text:
• Method and URL — required for web, API, and mobile assets; otherwise the form shows "Not required for the selected asset type".
  • Parameter (optional), Raw request (optional) (Burp / curl format), Request and Response.
  • Tool used (optional) and Environment (optional) (browser, OS, device, region).

docs.title: Saving and submitting
docs.text:
1. Click Create finding. The finding is saved as a Draft — "Saved as Draft. Promote to NEW for triage from the detail page." If anything is missing, the form lists it under "Please fix the following before submitting:".
  2. Open the draft, choose the submit action in the State actions panel, and click Confirm transition:
    • Pentest: Submit DRAFT for triage
    • Bug Bounty: Submit report for triage

docs.title: 5. Editing a finding
docs.text: Source When you can edit Notes Pentest (PTaaS) From Draft until the finding is Resolved Use Edit finding on the detail page. Severity and CVSS are locked once the finding is Verified. A Researcher edits only their own findings; a Lead Researcher can edit any finding on engagements they lead. Bug Bounty / VDP Only while it is a Draft Once submitted, the report is locked. Add clarifications as comments.

docs.title: Pentest (PTaaS) findings
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    DR([Draft]) -->|you submit| TR([Triaging])
    TR -->|lead or TPM verifies| V([Verified])
    V -->|client starts fixing| F([Fix in progress])
    F -->|client submits fix| R([Ready for retest])
    R -->|you confirm fix| D([Resolved])
    R -->|retest failed| F
    V -.->|client accepts risk| AR([Accepted risk])
State Meaning for you Draft Only you, your lead, and SecurityBoat can see it. Triaging Submitted; the lead researcher or TPM is validating severity, reproducibility, and scope. They may Request more information, or mark it as declined, duplicate, or out of scope with a reason. Verified Confirmed valid and now visible to the client. Fix in progress The client is fixing it. Ready for retest The client says the fix is deployed. Re-test it. Resolved You (or your lead) confirmed the fix with Confirm fix verified. Accepted risk The client formally accepted the risk instead of fixing it.

docs.title: Bug Bounty findings
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    DR([Draft]) -->|you submit| N([New])
    N --> T([Triaged])
    T -->|SB-Managed only| P([Pending Client Validation])
    P --> V([Verified])
    T --> V
    V --> F([Fix in Progress])
    F --> R([Retesting])

    R -->|retest failed| F

Bug Bounty reports can also be closed as Duplicate, Not Applicable, Informative, or Spam. Triage and retesting are done by SecurityBoat (SB-Managed programs) or the client's team (Self-Managed programs), not by researchers. See Bug Bounty Findings.

docs.title: 7. The finding detail page
docs.text:
• Header and stepper — severity, CVSS, state, source, and a stepper showing the current stage with a description.
  • Main column — Background, Description, Affected endpoint, Business impact, Remediation, HTTP request / response, Proof of concept, Comments, and the Timeline of state changes (10 per page, newest first).
  • Right column — State actions, the engagement or program card, Dates, Retest SLA, CVSS score, Classification, Risk assessment, OWASP Risk Rating, References, and Test context.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• Your comments are visible to Everyone on the finding.
  • Type @ to mention a participant.
  • You can edit your own comment for 15 minutes after posting, and delete it.
  • On a Resolved Bug Bounty finding, comments are locked for researchers.

docs.title: 8. From finding to payout
docs.text: A finding that is Verified on a paid program, or a completed pentest engagement, leads to a payout. Track it under Payouts.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Provide clear HTTP requests and responses — they speed up verification.
  • Complete all 11 CVSS metrics carefully — severity follows from them.
  • Double-check Bug Bounty reports before submitting — you cannot edit them afterwards.
  • Check for duplicates in the program's findings and Hacktivity before filing.
  • Retest promptly when a pentest finding reaches Ready for retest.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No Submit finding button The engagement is not in a testing state, or the Bug Bounty program is not Active. "Please fix the following before submitting" A required field is missing or too short. The list names each one. Severity field disabled Intentional; severity comes from the CVSS v4.0 metrics. No Edit finding button Bug Bounty reports lock once submitted; pentest findings lock once Resolved. Can't change severity on a pentest finding Severity and CVSS lock once the finding is Verified. My finding is stuck at New / Triaging Awaiting triage — add a polite comment if it has been a while. Marked duplicate Someone reported it first; check the comments.

docs.title: 1. Where you get paid
docs.text:
Payouts is your personal earnings page. It combines both sources of income:

  • Bug Bounty — a reward per verified finding on a paid program.
  • Pentest engagements — your researcher payout per engagement.

It tracks each payout from verification to payment and lets you download invoices. Statuses are view-only for researchers.

docs.title: Navigation

docs.title: 2. Earnings summary

Use the tabs All, Bug Bounty, and PTaaS (each with a count) to filter the table.

docs.title: 3. The payouts table
docs.text: Column Meaning Source BB (Bug Bounty) or PT (pentest). Description The finding title and ID (with severity and program), or the engagement title and Project ID. Click it for the payout detail page. Amount The payout amount and currency. Days Left For pentest payouts, the days until the payout becomes eligible, with the eligible date; Eligible once reached; "—" after payment. Check the payout detail page or contact SecurityBoat.

Before you can be paid: complete your bank details in Settings → Account and finish Identity Verification.

docs.title: Best practices

• Complete Identity Verification and bank details early.
  • Download invoices for your tax records as soon as they are available.

docs.title: Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause / Fix "No payouts yet" You have no verified paid findings or completed pentest payouts yet. Invoice shows "After approval" The payout is not approved yet. Pentest payout shows days left Pentest payouts become eligible 30 days after the engagement went live. Payment delayed Check your bank details and that your identity is Verified.

docs.title: 1. What it is and why it exists
docs.text:
Identity verification confirms you are a real, named person before SecurityBoat entrusts you with sensitive work and payments. It is an admin-initiated check: a SecurityBoat administrator requests it against your researcher profile, you complete a short document + face match flow on your phone, and once it passes your profile shows a Verified status to both you and SecurityBoat staff.

Verification is what unlocks platform capabilities such as payouts and premium work opportunities. You cannot start it yourself,it becomes available after an administrator requests it.

Data privacy & security: Verification is powered by third party identity provider, which performs the actual ID-document check and face match. SecurityBoat never sees or stores your raw documents it receives only the provider's structured result (document type, name, date of birth, a masked document number, face-match score, and the decision).

docs.title: 2. Verification process at a glance
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as SecurityBoat Admin
    participant R as You (Researcher)
    A->>R: Requests identity verification
    R->>R: Notification received +<br/>"Verify Identity" button appears
    R->>R: Click "Verify Identity"
    R->>R: Popup opens showing steps & QR code
    R->>R: Scan QR code on phone
    R->>R: Choose ID type + photograph<br/>document + face match
    R->>R: Complete mobile flow
    R-->>A: Outcome reconciled automatically
    A-->>R: Status: Approved / Pending Review / Declined

Verification statuses you may experience:

  • Not Requested: Initial state before an admin requests verification.
  • Requested: Verification has been requested by staff and a prompt is available.
  • In Progress: You have opened the flow and are uploading documents or completing face match on your phone.
  • Under Review: Verification completed and awaiting administrator sign-off.
  • Verified: Verification successful. "Verified" status active on your profile.
  • Resubmission Required: Staff requested you re-run the verification process with clearer inputs.
  • Declined: Verification check was rejected.
  • Expired / Incomplete: Session timed out or was closed before finishing.

docs.title: 3. Receiving the prompt
docs.text:
As soon as an administrator requests your verification, two things happen:

  1. You receive a notification (bell icon + email).
  2. An Identity verification prompt appears in two places on your Dashboard and on the dedicated Identity Verification page each with a Verification requested badge and a Verify Identity button.

On your Dashboard:

On the Identity Verification page (sidebar → Identity Verification):

docs.title: 4. Starting the check — the verification popup
docs.text:
Click Verify Identity (on either surface). SecurityBoat creates a secure verification session and opens a popup titled "Verification for My Application Complete these steps to verify your identity." It lists the required steps and displays a QR code; the badge status switches to In progress.

The verification process consists of two primary steps:

Step What happens ID verification You present an official government ID; the provider reads and validates it. Face verification You take a live selfie; the provider matches your live selfie to the ID photo.

Why a QR code? Document capture and liveness checks work best on a mobile camera. Scanning the QR code hands the session off to your mobile browser while keeping your desktop session active waiting for the result.

docs.title: 5. Completing the check on your phone
docs.text:
1. Scan the QR code using your phone's camera app to open the secure verification flow in your mobile browser.
  2. Choose your ID type — select your government-issued document type (e.g., passport, driving licence, national ID card).
  3. Capture your document — follow on-screen prompts to photograph your document clearly.
  4. Complete face match — take a live selfie so the system can verify your liveness and compare against your ID photo.
  5. Upon successful completion, the mobile interface reports success and the popup automatically closes.

SecurityBoat reconciles the signed outcome from the identity provider. Your status updates automatically to Verified or moves to Under Review if administrator review is required.

docs.title: 6. The verified state and status handling
Verified State
docs.text: Once approved, your Identity verification card displays a green Verified indicator (with approval date), and the Verify Identity button is removed. Staff can see your verified status on your profile.

docs.title: Handling Non-Passing Statuses
docs.text: Status you see What it means Action to take Verification was declined The verification check was rejected. Review the reason, ensure you use your own valid document, and click Verify Identity to try again. Additional information required Administrator requested a fresh submission with better quality inputs. Click Verify Identity to re-run the verification flow. Verification did not complete Session timed out or was closed prior to completion. Click Verify Identity to initiate a new verification session when ready.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Prepare documents and mobile device before clicking Verify Identity to prevent session timeouts.
  • Use valid, non-expired identification. Ensure the ID belongs to you; face matching compares your live selfie against the ID photograph.
  • Ensure good lighting and avoid glare. Clear document images and well-lit selfie captures reduce verification failures.
  • Complete verification promptly to unlock payouts and premium engagement opportunities without delay.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix No "Verify Identity" button available Verification has not yet been requested by an administrator. Verification is admin-initiated; the button appears once requested. "Could not start verification" error Session creation failed. Close the popup and click Verify Identity again. If issues persist, contact support. QR code will not scan Increase screen brightness and use native phone camera app. Keep the desktop browser window open. Completed mobile flow but status did not update Results reconcile automatically; refresh the page after a few moments. Declined despite correct documentation Verify that your ID is in date and your selfie was clear and unobscured. Click Verify Identity to retry or contact support.

docs.title: AI Assistant (Ish)
docs.text:
Security Researcher Guide · Researcher · Lead Researcher

The AI Assistant (powered by Ish / Ask Ish, TriNetra's agentic AI assistant layer) is a conversational assistant built into the researcher portal. Unlike generic AI chatbots, Ish is grounded in live platform data and strictly scoped to the engagements, findings, and bug bounty programs you participate in.

docs.title: 1. What Ish is for Researchers
docs.text:
As a researcher, managing multiple engagements, tracking finding triage, and verifying testing coverage can require switching between multiple views.

Ish provides an instant, plain-language interface to help you: * Track the review status of your submitted vulnerabilities. * Rapidly review engagement scope, target endpoints, and Rules of Engagement (RoE). * Identify untested methodology items on engagement coverage checklists. * Check payout clearances and hold period statuses.

graph TD
    A[Researcher Question] --> B(Ish AI Layer)
    C[Engagement Scope / RoE] --> B
    D[Your Findings & Submissions] --> B
    E[Your Payout & Coverage Data] --> B
    B --> F[Grounded Answer + Direct Screen Links]

docs.title: Access Modes
docs.text:
• Sidebar Navigation: Click AI Assistant in the main sidebar to open the dedicated conversational interface for multi-turn queries and history.
  • Contextual Widget: Click the floating Ask Ish widget on any engagement or finding screen to ask questions relevant to your active view.

docs.title: Security & Privacy Boundaries
docs.text:
• Strict Personal Scoping: Ish strictly isolates researcher data. You can only query findings you authored, engagements you are seated on, and your own payouts. You can never see other researchers' earnings or private submissions.
  • Confidentiality: Queries and context are processed within TriNetra's secure tenant boundary and are never used to train public LLM models.
  • Model Transparency: Every answer displays a Model Badge and Token Count to provide full visibility into the underlying model.

docs.title: Finding Triage & Verification
docs.text:
• "Which of my submitted findings are currently in TPM Review?"
  • "Show me all drafts I have saved across active engagements."
  • "Have any of my findings been marked as 'Needs More Info' by the triage team?"

docs.title: Engagement Scope & Rules of Engagement
docs.text:
• "Summarise the in-scope assets and testing windows for Engagement #104."
  • "Are subdomains outside of *.api.example.com in scope for this bug bounty program?"
  • "What are the prohibited testing techniques listed in the engagement brief?"

docs.title: Methodology & Coverage Checklists
docs.text:
• "What items on the Web Application checklist for my current engagement are still marked untested?"
  • "Summarise the overall coverage progress for the API security section."

docs.title: Payouts & Compensation
docs.text:
• "Which of my verified findings have cleared the hold period and are eligible for payout?"
  • "What is my total pending payout amount for this month?"

docs.title: 4. Best Practices & Operational Security
docs.text:
• OpSec & Data Safety: Never paste production passwords, live session tokens, customer PII, or raw weaponized exploit payloads into the chat.
  • Scope Verification: Use Ish as a quick scope reference, but always double-check the official Brief tab for legally binding engagement constraints.
  • Direct Action: Follow the deep links provided by Ish to open finding cards, retest workflows, or payout invoice screens.

docs.title: 5. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Probable Cause Recommended Fix "I cannot find that engagement/finding" The item is outside your assigned engagements or has not been authored by you. Confirm you are seated on the engagement in your Pentest Engagements list. Response seems outdated Status changed in another tab (e.g. finding verified by TPM). Ask Ish to re-query the latest status or open the Findings tab directly. Model returns unexpected response Complex question with ambiguous scope. Specify the exact Engagement Title or Finding ID in your query.

docs.title: 3. MFA Setup
docs.text: Manage multi-factor authentication (MFA) to secure your account. Because your profile carries sensitive findings, signed contracts, and bank payout details, maintaining active MFA is highly recommended.

docs.title: How to Enroll in MFA
docs.text:
1. Open Setup: Navigate to Settings → MFA Setup and click Setup MFA.
  2. Scan QR Code: Open your preferred authenticator app (e.g., Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator, or 1Password) and scan the displayed QR code. If your device cannot scan the code, click Show to reveal the secret key and enter it manually.
  3. Save/Copy Key: You can also click the copy icon to securely copy the configuration key to your clipboard.
  4. Complete Enrollment: Once you have scanned or entered the code into your authenticator app, click the Done — I've added it to my app button. The app will confirm your enrollment, and you will be prompted for your MFA verification code during your next login attempt.

docs.title: Disabling or Resetting MFA
docs.text:
If you currently have MFA enabled and need to re-key or disable it:

  1. Navigate to Settings → MFA Setup.
  2. Click the red Reset MFA button.
  3. Confirming this action removes all active MFA factors from your account immediately. You can now log in using only your email and password, or begin the enrollment flow again.

docs.title: Recovery & Lost Authenticator Access
docs.text:
If you lose access to your authenticator app, you can reset your MFA using the self-service flow:

  • Request recovery: Click the Reset MFA link on the login page, enter your registered email, and follow the link sent to your inbox.
  • Administrative assistance: If you cannot access your email, contact the SecurityBoat support team to verify your identity and manually reset your MFA settings from the administration panel.

docs.title: 4. Payouts
docs.text: The Payouts tab is your earnings dashboard — see the dedicated Payouts guide.

docs.title: 5. Availability
docs.text:
The Availability tab (My availability) is where you tell SecurityBoat when you can take pentest work: "Mark the date ranges you are available for pentest work. Any day you have not marked is treated as unavailable."

  1. Pick a From and To date. Past dates cannot be selected — the earliest date is today.
  2. Add an optional Note.
  3. Save the range.

The calendar shows a rolling two-month window from today. Days you marked show as Available; everything else is Unavailable. Recent past days appear greyed out for context only.

docs.title: 6. Notifications
docs.text: Choose which notifications reach you and how. Keep invite/finding/payout notifications on so you don't miss opportunities, verification requests, or payment updates. Critical security alerts may bypass these settings.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Complete bank details + verification first — nothing pays out without them.
  • Keep skills/certifications current — they drive marketplace matches and your public profile.
  • Enable MFA.

Profile not on the directory Ensure your profile is complete and Profile visibility is public. Can't edit my name Your identity is verified, which locks the name. Contact an administrator.
