docs.title: Disclosure Requests (Researcher View)
docs.text:
A disclosure request asks for one of your resolved Bug Bounty or VDP findings to be published on the public Hacktivity feed.

Researchers do not have a Disclosure Requests page in the sidebar. You request disclosure from the program's Findings tab, and you are notified when your request is reviewed. The review itself is handled by the TPM and the client.

docs.title: Which findings can be disclosed
docs.text:
• Only your own findings.
  • Only findings that are Resolved (or closed as Not Applicable). Open, verified, or in-progress findings cannot be disclosed.
  • Only one active request per finding. If a request is rejected, you can request again.

docs.title: Requesting disclosure
docs.text:
1. Open the program and go to its Findings tab.
  2. Find your resolved finding. In the Actions column, click Request Publish.
  3. You'll see "Publish request submitted — awaiting review", and the column changes to Requested.

docs.title: The request lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Request Publish] --> B([Awaiting TPM Review])
    B -->|TPM approves| C([Awaiting Client Approval])
    B -->|TPM rejects| D([Rejected])
    C -->|client approves| E([Published])
    C -->|client rejects| D
    D -.->|request again| A
Status What you see in the Actions column Awaiting TPM Review / Awaiting Client Approval Requested Published Published — click it to open the public disclosure page Rejected Request Publish appears again so you can resubmit

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Be patient — the request is reviewed by two parties.
  • Don't take rejection personally — clients may have confidentiality or regulatory reasons.
  • Check Hacktivity to see your published disclosures.

← Previous: Hacktivity | Next: Agentic Pentest →

docs.title: Hacktivity
docs.text: Hacktivity is the public feed of disclosed vulnerabilities from bug bounty programs. It appears under Bug Bounty in the sidebar. Published disclosures earn you public recognition for responsible disclosure and build your professional reputation.

docs.title: Accessing Hacktivity
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a Researcher
  2. In the sidebar, under OPERATIONS, click Hacktivity

docs.title: What Appears Here
docs.text: Publicly disclosed vulnerabilities from bug bounty programs. Each entry includes the finding title, severity, CVSS score, technical description, researcher attribution, and publication date. The feed is ordered with the most recent disclosures first.

docs.title: How Disclosures Get Here
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[You discover +<br/>report vuln] --> B[Finding triaged,<br/>validated, resolved]
    B --> C[You submit<br/>Disclosure Request]
    C --> D[TPM reviews<br/>technical accuracy]
    D --> E[Client approves<br/>disclosure]
    E --> F[Published on Hacktivity<br/>with your name]

docs.title: Why Hacktivity Matters for Researchers
docs.text:
• Reputation — your name and findings are publicly visible, building credibility for future engagements and bug bounty invites
  • Portfolio — each published disclosure becomes part of your professional track record
  • Community — contributes to the broader security community's knowledge base
  • Recognition — demonstrates your expertise to potential clients and programme managers

docs.title: Tips for Researchers
docs.text:
• Write clear, educational disclosures — focus on the technical finding, not the client
  • Redact any sensitive client-identifying information unless explicitly authorised
  • Submit disclosure requests promptly after a finding is resolved
  • A well-written disclosure with clear reproduction steps and impact analysis is more likely to be approved

← Previous: Bug Bounty | Next: Disclosure Requests →

docs.title: 1. What Feedback is for
docs.text:
The Feedback module is a platform-wide dialog that lets you submit bug reports and feature requests directly to the Tri-Netra issue tracker. It is available to all roles and serves as the primary channel for reporting platform issues or suggesting improvements.

The Feedback module is not a live support channel. For urgent blockers — such as an engagement that will not load or a payout that has stalled — contact your TPM or Lead Researcher directly.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: The Feedback button sits at the bottom of the sidebar, below all other navigation items. It is always visible regardless of which page you are viewing.

docs.title: 2. The Feedback Dialog
docs.text:
Clicking Feedback opens a modal dialog with the following fields:

Field Required Description Kind Yes Radio buttons: Bug (report something broken) or Feature Request (suggest an enhancement). Title Yes A concise, one-line summary of the issue or request. Severity No Dropdown: Low, Medium, High, or Critical. Only relevant for bug reports. Description Yes A detailed explanation — include steps to reproduce, expected behaviour, and actual behaviour. Current page Auto-filled The URL of the page you were on when you opened the dialog. The engineering team sees exactly where you encountered the issue. You can edit this if needed. Console excerpt No Optional — paste any errors from your browser's developer console (F12 → Console tab). Helps diagnose front-end issues.

The Submit button remains disabled until Kind, Title, and Description are all filled.

docs.title: 3. When to use each kind
docs.text:
Use Bug when… Use Feature Request when… Something that previously worked has broken You want new functionality that does not exist yet A feature behaves differently than documented An existing feature could be improved or extended You receive an error message or unexpected result You need a new filter, sort, or view option Data displays incorrectly or inconsistently A workflow is missing a step that would help you A page fails to load or times out You have an idea that would make the platform more productive

When in doubt, choose Bug if the platform is not working as you reasonably expect it to. Choose Feature Request if it works as designed but you wish it did more.

docs.title: 4. Researcher-specific scenarios
docs.text:
These are common situations researchers encounter and the recommended submission type:

Scenario Kind Notes Agentic Pentest discovery feed not updating Bug Note which engagement and whether the Live Recon tab or Human Review Queue is affected. AI Red Teaming engagement not loading Bug Include the engagement name. If it is time-sensitive, also notify your TPM. Finding shows incorrect severity in the UI Bug Mention the finding ID and the severity you believe is correct. Ask Ish returns irrelevant or incorrect responses Bug Paste the question you asked and the response you received. Need a new filter or sort option in the findings list Feature Request Describe the filter/sort you need and why it would help your workflow. Sign-off workflow missing a step Feature Request Explain what step is missing and where in the process it belongs. Dashboard metrics do not match the findings list Bug Reference both views so the team can cross-check. Want a dark mode or UI theme option Feature Request These are valid — the product team reviews all submissions.

docs.title: 5. Writing an effective bug report
docs.text:
A well-written bug report saves the engineering team time and gets your issue resolved faster. Every report should answer three questions: what happened, what you expected, and how to reproduce it.

Example — good bug report:

Kind: Bug Title: Agentic Pentest discovery feed stops updating after switching engagements Severity: High Description: - Steps to reproduce: Open Agentic Pentest → select Engagement A from the dropdown → observe the Live Recon feed updating normally → switch to Engagement B → the feed freezes and shows the last entries from Engagement A. - Expected behaviour: The feed should refresh to show the discovery activity for Engagement B. - Actual behaviour: The feed remains frozen on Engagement A's data until the page is manually refreshed. - Impact: I cannot monitor live discoveries when working across multiple engagements. Current page: (auto-captured) Console excerpt: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at FeedComponent.updateFeed

Example — poor bug report:

Kind: Bug Title: Feed broken Description: The feed doesn't work. Please fix.

The poor report gives the engineering team nothing to work with. Always include steps, expected behaviour, and actual behaviour.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Submit one issue per report. Do not bundle multiple bugs or feature requests into a single submission — each needs its own tracking and resolution.
  • Be specific and actionable. Include reproduction steps, expected vs actual behaviour, and the impact on your work.
  • Use the auto-captured URL. The Current page field tells the engineering team exactly where the problem occurred. Only edit it if the captured page is wrong.
  • Include console errors for front-end issues. Open your browser's developer tools (F12), go to the Console tab, and copy any red error messages into the Console excerpt field. This is often the fastest way to diagnose UI bugs.
  • Choose severity honestly. Reserve Critical for issues that completely block your ability to work (e.g., cannot submit findings, cannot access engagements). Use High for major functional breaks with no workaround.
  • For feature requests, explain the "why". Describe the problem you are trying to solve, not just the solution you envision. The product team may find a better approach.
  • Do not use Feedback for urgent support. The issue tracker is not monitored in real time. If an engagement deadline is at risk, contact your TPM or Lead Researcher directly.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix Submit button stays disabled At least one required field (Kind, Title, Description) is empty. Fill all three to enable the button. Not sure whether to submit a Bug or Feature Request Refer to the table in section 3. If still unsure, default to Bug — the triage team can reclassify it. Issue is blocking your work right now Feedback is not a live support channel. Submit the bug report for tracking, then contact your TPM or Lead Researcher for immediate help. Need to follow up on a previous submission Feedback submissions go to the Tri-Netra issue tracker. Your TPM can look up the status of your ticket. Not sure what to put in Console excerpt Open DevTools (F12), click the Console tab, and look for red error lines. Copy those — even a partial stack trace is helpful. If the console is clean, leave the field empty.

← Previous: AI Assistant (Ish) | Next: Team Feedback →

docs.title: Team Feedback
docs.text:
Team Feedback is where you rate the researchers you worked with and the pentest itself, once a pentest is complete — "Rate the researchers you worked with on completed pentests. Your feedback is private — only you and platform admins can see it."

This is different from the Feedback button at the bottom of the sidebar, which sends product feedback to SecurityBoat. See Feedback.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Click Team Feedback in the sidebar (Researcher / Lead Researcher). The page lists your pentests that are Delivered, in Remediation, or Closed. Click one to open its feedback wizard.

docs.title: The three-step wizard
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[1. Peer Review] --> B[2. Pentest Process] --> C[3. Pentest Scope] --> D[Submit]

docs.title: Step 1 — Peer Review
docs.text:
Rate each teammate on five parameters, from 1 to 5 stars:

Parameter What you are rating Responsiveness How promptly and reliably they responded and followed up. Vulnerability Quality The quality of their findings and write-ups. Technical Expertise Their technical depth on this pentest. Engagement Delivery How well they delivered their part of the engagement. Communication & Professionalism How clearly and professionally they communicated.
  • All five parameters must be scored before you can save.
  • Add a comment — "Share what your peer could improve and what worked well". A comment is required if any score is 4 or below.
  • Saved feedback shows a Feedback given badge. You can update or delete it later.

docs.title: Step 2 — Pentest Process
docs.text: Rate the pentest process overall, pick what went well and what to improve from the suggested points (a point can only be in one list), and add a note. Continue is enabled once you have given a rating.

docs.title: Step 3 — Pentest Scope
docs.text: The wizard shows the scope from the brief — the asset, its types, and the in-scope and out-of-scope notes — and asks: "Did the scope outlined in the brief accurately reflect the actual testing performed?" Answer underscoped (more testing was needed), accurately scoped, or overscoped (the brief claimed more than was relevant), and add an optional note. Then submit steps 2 and 3 together.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
• Your feedback is visible only to you and SecurityBoat platform administrators.
  • You never see feedback that other researchers wrote about you.

← Previous: Feedback | Next: Settings →

docs.title: Researcher & Lead Researcher Guide
docs.text:
Version 4.2 — August 2026 · Production guide for live users · en-GB

This guide is for Researchers and Lead Researchers — the people who perform the security testing: joining engagements, hunting vulnerabilities, and authoring findings. Everything is scoped to you — your engagements, your findings, and your pay.

docs.title: Chapters
docs.text:
# Chapter What it covers 0 Getting Started Overview and initial onboarding workflow for Researchers. 1 Introduction Your role, personal scope, and the modules you can access. 2 Logging In Single Sign-On (SSO) end to end — application, invite, MFA, sessions. 3 Dashboard Your work hub — active engagements, open findings, pay. 4 Opportunities Open engagement opportunities you can apply for. 5 Invites Direct invitations to join engagements. 6 Engagements The engagements you're seated on — scope, team, timeline. 7 Findings Vulnerabilities on your engagements. 8 My Findings The findings you personally authored. 9 Payouts Your earnings and payout history (your scope only). 10 Identity Verification Complete verification to unlock paid work. 11 Bug Bounty Programs you participate in — submit and track reports. 12 Hacktivity Public feed of disclosed vulnerability reports. 11a My Credentials Test credentials assigned to you and your credential requests. 13 Disclosure Requests Request publication of your resolved findings from a program's Findings tab. 14 Agentic Pentest Direct and validate AI-driven recon & exploit swarms. 15 AI Red Teaming Assess LLM safety, prompt injection, and cross-tenant isolation. 16 AI Assistant (Ish) Ask Ish about your engagements, scope, and findings. 17 Feedback Submit platform bug reports and feature requests. 17a Team Feedback Rate teammates, the pentest process, and the scope on completed pentests. 18 Settings Account, public profile, bank details, MFA, availability, and notifications.

Not available to Researchers: Clients, Assets, ASM, Reports, Compliance, Integrations, and Admin. Pay is always your own scope — never shared across researchers. Lead Researchers get an enhanced dashboard and team view on top of everything above.

Start with Getting Started →

docs.title: My Credentials
docs.text:
My Credentials lists the test accounts assigned to you for Bug Bounty programs and the status of your credential requests — "Test accounts assigned to you for bug bounty programs, and the status of your requests."

To open it, click My Credentials in the sidebar. You request credentials from a program's Scope tab — see Scope → Test credentials.

docs.title: Assignments
docs.text:
Column What it shows Program / asset The program (linked) and the asset the credentials belong to Roles The account roles in the set (for example admin, user) Status Active, Released, or Revoked Assigned / Ended When the assignment started and ended Actions Reveal credentials, Report issue, and Release
  • Reveal credentials shows the usernames, passwords, and notes. They hide automatically after a short countdown, when you switch tabs, or when you leave the page.
  • Report issue tells the program team that a credential does not work.
  • Release ends your access immediately: "You lose access to the credentials for this asset immediately and cannot view them again. Release when you have finished testing."

If credentials cannot be revealed, the row explains why: Access released/revoked, Program paused — credentials cannot be viewed, You no longer have access to this program, or Credentials unavailable.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
Column What it shows Program / asset Where you asked for credentials Reason What you wrote in the request Status Pending review, Approved — waiting for credentials, Credentials assigned, Rejected (with the reason), or Cancelled Submitted / Decision When you asked and when it was decided Actions Cancel while the request is still open

A request can be cancelled automatically if you no longer meet the program's requirements.

docs.title: Reported issues
docs.text: Each issue you reported shows its category, your message, its status (Open, Acknowledged, Resolved), and the review note once resolved.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Fix "No credentials assigned" Request credentials from an active program's Scope tab. Approved requests appear here. Reveal credentials is missing The assignment ended, the program is paused, or you lost access. The row shows the reason. My request was rejected Read the rejection reason, adjust your justification, and submit a new request.

← Previous: Integrations | Next: Agentic Pentest →

docs.title: Bug Bounty & VDP Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to the Bug Bounty & VDP module on the Tri-Netra platform. This guide helps you find programs, test within scope, and submit vulnerability reports.

Bug Bounty testing is self-directed and continuous, complementing scheduled, team-based pentest engagements. You browse programs, review their policies, test in-scope targets, submit reports, and earn rewards or reputation points.

Access: the BB Program, My Credentials, and Hacktivity entries appear in your sidebar when Bug Bounty is enabled for your account.

docs.title: Testing workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Browse BB Program list] --> B{Program visibility}
    B -->|Public| C[Read scope and rules]
    B -->|Private| D[Accept the invitation on Invites]
    D --> C
    C --> E[Optional: request test credentials]
    E --> F[Test in-scope assets]
    C --> F
    F --> G[Submit finding: saved as Draft]
    G --> H[Submit report for triage]
    H --> I[Triage by SecurityBoat or the client team]
    I -->|Verified| J{Program type}
    J -->|Bug Bounty| K[Cash reward + reputation points]
    J -->|VDP| L[Swag / Hall of Fame + reputation points]

docs.title: Bug Bounty
docs.text: • Incentives: severity-tiered cash rewards (P1–P5) plus reputation points.

docs.title: VDP (Vulnerability Disclosure Program)
docs.text: • Incentives: recognition — swag, Hall of Fame placement, and reputation points. No cash reward.

docs.title: Who triages: the management badge
docs.text:
Every program shows a management badge. Hover over it to read what it means.

Badge Who reviews your reports SB-Managed SecurityBoat's team reviews and manages the findings. Self-Managed The client's own team reviews and manages the findings. SecurityBoat is not involved in triage.

docs.title: Program visibility and access
docs.text:
• Public programs: open to all eligible researchers. You can start testing in-scope assets without an invitation.
  • Private programs: invite-only. Invitations appear on your Invites page with the status Pending. Once you accept, the program opens for you.

If you are removed from a private program, you lose access to the program and can no longer submit findings to it.

docs.title: Program states
docs.text:
State What you can do Active Testing is live. Review the scope, test, and submit findings. Scheduled Approved and going live on its start date. Submissions open when it becomes Active. Deactivated Paused. You can read the program and your past findings, but new findings are not accepted. Ended The program has finished. Read-only.

Only Active programs accept new findings.

docs.title: Browsing programs
docs.text:
Click BB Program in the main sidebar.

Element What it shows KPI tiles Total programs, Active, and Awaiting review Type tabs All Programs, VDP, Bug Bounty State filter All States plus one pill per state Search Search by program name… Table Program, Client, Type, Management, Visibility, Status, Findings

Your filters and page are kept in the page address, so Back returns you to the same view.

Note

Click a program to open its Program Detail view and its tabs.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Complete Identity Verification early. It is required for paid work and payouts.
  • Read the Scope tab carefully, including the In scope and Out of scope notes. Out-of-scope reports earn no reward or points.
  • Check Hacktivity and the program Leaderboard to avoid duplicates.
  • Read the Updates tab for scope changes or reward announcements.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause / Solution Cannot see a specific program It is Private and you have not been invited, your invitation is still Pending, or you were removed. Check Invites. No Submit finding button The program is not Active (Scheduled, Deactivated, or Ended). No monetary reward shown The program is a VDP. Rewards are swag, points, and Hall of Fame.

← Previous: Identity Verification | Next: Program Details Overview →

docs.title: Activity
docs.text: The Activity tab provides a read-only, chronological log of events related to the Bug Bounty or VDP program. It helps researchers track historical changes, updates, and scope adjustments.

docs.title: Logged Events
docs.text:
The activity log records the following milestones:

Event Type Description Program Status Updates Changes in program state (e.g., when a program is activated, paused, or closed). Scope Changes Notifications of newly added assets, URL shifts, or assets moved out-of-scope. Reward Scale Updates Increases or adjustments to the reward ranges. New Updates Published Logs when a new announcement is posted on the Updates tab. Submissions & Payouts Broad entries confirming finding submissions or payout confirmations.

Note

Out of respect for researcher privacy, finding details, specific reporter names, and payout specifics are anonymized or hidden from the general activity log.

← Previous: Payouts | Next: Leaderboard →

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
The Chat tab is a messaging channel between you, the client's team, and SecurityBoat.

Private programs only. Researchers see the Chat tab on Private programs they have joined. Public programs have no Chat tab for researchers — use the Updates tab for announcements.

docs.title: Sending messages
docs.text:
• Your messages are always posted to Everyone (everyone in this chat).
  • Type @ to mention a participant. They get a notification.
  • The client and SecurityBoat can also post messages for their own audiences, which you do not see.

docs.title: Chat guidelines
docs.text:
Guideline Rule Do not share findings Never paste vulnerability details, PoC code, or exploits in chat. Submit them through Submit finding. Use it for scope questions Ask before testing anything you are unsure about. Be professional Keep a polite, professional tone. Keep it relevant Short questions about the program's scope and testing.

← Previous: Updates | Next: Integrations →

docs.title: Collaborators
docs.text: The Collaborators tab lists the registered researchers who are actively participating in the program.

docs.title: Collaborator List
docs.text:
The tab provides a roster of participants, allowing you to see your fellow security testers:

Column Description Username The researcher's platform handle. Role Displays the researcher's classification (e.g., Researcher, Lead Researcher). Verification Status Shows if the researcher's identity has been verified.

docs.title: Cooperation Guidelines
docs.text:
While researchers compete for findings and rewards, the Collaborators tab fosters a shared community. When testing, you must follow these cooperation guidelines:

Rule Guideline Requirement Fair Testing Do not attempt to disrupt or block other researchers' testing activities. Confidentiality In private invite-only programs, all program details, targets, and findings are strictly confidential and must not be shared.

← Previous: Leaderboard | Next: Updates →

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: The Findings tab lists your own submissions to this program. It is also where you open the Submit finding drawer.

docs.title: Your submissions
docs.text:
Four tiles summarise your reports: Total findings, Awaiting triage, In remediation, and Resolved. Use the All Findings and Triage (n) sub-tabs to switch between everything and reports still awaiting triage.

Column Description Finding Title and finding ID. Severity Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Informational. State Current lifecycle state, plus a closure label (e.g. Duplicate, Not Applicable) when one applies. Researcher You. Jira The client's linked Jira issue, if any. Submitted Submission date. Actions Request Publish for disclosure-eligible findings, or the disclosure status.

Click a row to open the finding's detail page.

docs.title: How to submit a finding
docs.text:
The Submit finding button appears only while the program is Active.

  1. Click Submit finding. A drawer opens — "Report a vulnerability to (program name)".
  2. Fill in the form (the same form used for pentests; see Findings → Submitting a finding). Required fields include the title, vulnerability type, VRT category, CWE, all 11 CVSS v4.0 metrics, the writeup sections, CIA impact, OWASP likelihood and impact, the endpoint (for web, API, and mobile assets), and at least one reference URL.
  3. Click Create finding. The finding is saved as a Draft — the footer reads "Saved as Draft. Promote to NEW for triage from the detail page."
  4. Open the draft and use State actions → Submit report for triage to send it.

Submitted reports are locked

You can edit a Bug Bounty report only while it is a Draft. Once you submit it for triage, you can no longer change its content. Add clarifications as comments instead.

docs.title: The report lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    DR([Draft]) -->|you submit| N([New])
    N --> T([Triaged])
    T -->|SB-Managed only| P([Pending Client Validation])
    P --> V([Verified])
    T --> V
    V --> F([Fix in Progress])
    F --> R([Retesting])
    R --> D([Resolved])
    R -->|retest failed| F

A report can also be closed from any open state as Duplicate or Not Applicable, and may end as Informative or Spam.

State Meaning for you Draft Only you can see it. Edit freely, then submit. New Submitted and awaiting initial review. Triaged Initial review done; detailed validation in progress. Pending Client Validation SB-Managed programs: referred to the client to confirm. Verified Confirmed as a legitimate, reproducible issue. Rewards are based on this. Fix in Progress The client is fixing it. Retesting The fix is being verified by the triage team. Resolved Fixed and retested. You can now request disclosure. Duplicate / Not Applicable / Informative / Spam Closed without a reward. Check the comments for the reason.

Triage is done by SecurityBoat on SB-Managed programs and by the client's team on Self-Managed programs. If the triager asks for more information, use Provide requested information in the State actions panel.

On a Resolved report, comments are locked for researchers.

docs.title: Requesting disclosure
docs.text:
When your finding is Resolved (or closed as Not Applicable), a Request Publish button appears in the Actions column.

flowchart LR
    A[Request Publish] --> B([Requested])
    B -->|TPM, then client approves| C([Published])
    B -->|rejected| A
  • Requested — your request is under review: first by the TPM, then by the client.
  • Published — the disclosure is live on Hacktivity. Click it to open the public page.
  • If a request is rejected, you can request again.

You are notified when your request is reviewed.

← Previous: Rewards | Next: Payouts →

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: The Integrations tab lists third-party tools that have been linked to this program by the client organization.

docs.title: Active Integrations
docs.text: While researchers do not configure integrations, you can see which tools are connected (e.g., Jira).

docs.title: Jira Integration
docs.text:
When Jira is connected and active:

  • Once your submitted finding moves to the Verified state, it is automatically pushed as an issue ticket to the client's internal Jira board.
  • This ensures fast visibility for the client's developers, speeding up the patch lifecycle and expediting your payouts.
  • Status updates in the client's Jira system can sync back, updating the finding state on the Tri-Netra platform automatically.

The diagram below illustrates the automated Jira synchronization flow:

graph LR
    Sub[Submit Finding] --> Ver[TPM Verifies Finding]
    Ver --> Jira[Jira Ticket Created Automatically]
    Jira --> Dev[Client Developer Patches Bug]
    Dev --> Sync[Status Syncs Back to Tri-Netra]

← Previous: Chat | Next: My Credentials →

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text: The Leaderboard tab highlights the top-performing researchers who have successfully submitted valid findings to this program. It drives peer recognition and gamifies the testing process.

docs.title: Leaderboard Rankings
docs.text: Researchers are ranked based on the total Reputation Points earned on this specific program. The tab features:

docs.title: The Top 3 Podium
docs.text: A visually prominent section highlighting the three highest-scoring researchers for the current filter window.

docs.title: Detailed Ranking Table
docs.text:
Lists all contributing researchers. The columns include:

Column Description Rank Numeric position. Researcher Platform username and avatar. Reputation Points Total points earned on this program. Accepted Submissions Count of valid findings verified by the TPM. Rewards Earned Swag tier or total monetary rewards.

docs.title: Filter Options
docs.text:
You can filter the leaderboard to track activity over different periods:

Filter Scope Today Ranks researchers by points earned in the last 24 hours. This Week Focuses on the current calendar week. All Time Accumulates all points since the program was launched.

docs.title: Why Leaderboard Standing Matters
docs.text:
Your position on leaderboards directly affects your opportunities on the platform:

Benefit How It Works Private Program Invites Organizations hosting high-payout, private Bug Bounty programs inspect leaderboards to select which researchers to invite. Reputation & Trust Top-ranked researchers are selected as Lead Researchers for scheduled PTaaS engagements.

← Previous: Activity | Next: Collaborators →

docs.title: Program Detail Overview
docs.text: When you open a Bug Bounty or VDP program, you land on the Program Detail view — your portal for testing and tracking submissions for that program.

docs.title: Page layout
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    P[Program Detail page] --> H[Header: status, visibility, type, management and Safe Harbor badges]
    P --> S[Lifecycle stepper]
    P --> K[KPI tiles]
    P --> T[Tabs]
    T --> O[Overview: details, management model, stats, Hall of Fame]
    T --> X[Scope, Rewards, Findings, Activity, Leaderboard, Collaborators, Updates, Chat, Integrations]

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
Element Description Program code A short reference in a pill badge (e.g. BB-ACS-01). Status Active, Scheduled, Deactivated, or Ended. Visibility Public or Private. Type VDP or Bug Bounty. Management badge SB-Managed (triaged by SecurityBoat) or Self-Managed (triaged by the client's team). Hover for the explanation. Safe Harbor badge Shown when the program publishes a safe-harbor policy. The policy text is on the Scope tab. Program name and organisation The full name and the owning organisation.

Below the header, a lifecycle stepper shows the program's progress (Approved → Scheduled → Active → Ended).

If the program is Deactivated or Ended, a notice explains that new findings are not being accepted, while existing findings, scope, and updates remain available.

docs.title: KPI tiles
docs.text: Tile Description Total bounties paid Cumulative cash paid out (Bug Bounty), or Recognition — VDP — swag + HoF. Reports received Total findings submitted to the program by all researchers. Active since The program's start date.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
Your selected tab is kept in the page address.

Tab What it contains Overview Program details, management model, stats, and the Hall of Fame. Scope In-scope assets, scope notes, rules of engagement, safe harbor, and test credential requests. Rewards Reward ranges (P1–P5) or recognition rules. Findings Your submissions to this program and the Submit finding button. Activity Program milestones (scope updates, state changes). Leaderboard Top researchers on this program. Collaborators Researchers who have submitted findings to the program. Updates Official announcements from the program team. Chat Private programs only. Messaging with the program team. Integrations Connected integrations such as Jira (information only).

Researchers do not see the Team or Payouts tabs. Track your rewards under My Payouts in the sidebar.

docs.title: Program details
docs.text: Field Description Program ID, Type, Status, Visibility, Organisation, Managed by Identification of the program. Start date / End date The program window. End date reads Continuous if open-ended. Hall of Fame Enabled or Disabled. Reward structure P1–P5 reward chips, or the VDP recognition note.

docs.title: Management model
docs.text: A card repeats the badge with a one-line explanation of who triages your reports.

docs.title: Program stats
docs.text: Cell Description Total All findings submitted to the program. Triage Findings awaiting review. Accepted Confirmed vulnerabilities being remediated. Resolved Fixed findings. Discarded Reports closed as duplicate, not applicable, or invalid.

docs.title: Hall of Fame
docs.text:
If enabled, a podium shows the top three researchers. Filter by Today, This Week, or All Time. Until findings are accepted, it reads: "No researchers on the leaderboard yet. Top contributors will appear once findings are accepted."

← Previous: Bug Bounty Overview | Next: Scope →

docs.title: Payouts
docs.text:
Researchers do not have a Payouts tab on the program page. That tab is used by the client and SecurityBoat to approve rewards.

Your rewards from every program appear in My Payouts in the sidebar (also under Settings → Payouts). See the Payouts guide.

docs.title: How a Bug Bounty reward reaches you
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    V([Verified]) --> A([Approved by SB Admin])
    A --> PI([Payment Initiated]) --> TA([Transaction Approved]) --> PD([Payment Done])
  • Verified — your finding is verified and the reward is waiting for approval. On a Self-Managed program, the client approves first and then SecurityBoat; on an SB-Managed program, SecurityBoat approves.
  • Approved by SB Admin — the reward is approved and your invoice can be downloaded.
  • Payment Initiated → Transaction Approved → Payment Done — the payment is being made and then completed.

VDP programs award reputation points instead of money. They appear on the program's Leaderboard.

← Previous: Findings | Next: Activity →

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text: The Rewards tab defines the incentive structure of the program. Depending on whether the program is a Bug Bounty or a VDP, rewards may consist of monetary payouts, reputation points, or recognition swag.

docs.title: Monetary Payout Grid (Bug Bounty)
docs.text:
For paid Bug Bounty programs, rewards are structured into a tier-based grid matching the severity classification of findings. Severity is determined using the CVSS v4.0 score calculated during submission:

Severity Level CVSS v4.0 Range Standard Reward Range (Example) P1 — Critical 9.0 – 10.0 \$1,500 – \$3,000+ P2 — High 7.0 – 8.9 \$800 – \$1,499 P3 — Medium 4.0 – 6.9 \$300 – \$799 P4 — Low 0.1 – 3.9 \$100 – \$299 P5 — Informational 0.0 Swag / Points Only

Tip

The amounts above are only an example. Each program's reward amounts (a single amount or a range per severity) are set by SecurityBoat for that program. Always refer to the live grid on the Rewards tab.

docs.title: Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) Recognition
docs.text:
VDPs do not offer cash payouts. Instead, they reward valid contributions through:

  • Swag: T-shirts, stickers, or branded merchandise shipped to your verified address.
  • Hall of Fame: Public listing on the program overview page, displaying top-performing researchers.
  • Certificates: A formal certificate of appreciation detailing your contribution.

docs.title: Reputation Points System
docs.text:
Accepted findings award Reputation Points based on severity: P1 Critical earns the most and P5 Informational the least. The points per severity are set platform-wide by SecurityBoat and are the same on every program; the program's Rewards tab shows the current values. Reputation points decide your ranking on the program Leaderboard.

flowchart LR
    F[Accepted finding] --> S{Severity}
    S --> P1[P1 Critical: most points]
    S --> P3[P2–P4: fewer points]
    S --> P5[P5 Informational: fewest points]

← Previous: Scope | Next: Findings →

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The Scope tab is the formal contract between you and the client organisation. It defines exactly what you are authorised to test and what is off-limits.

docs.title: In-scope assets
docs.text:
Each in-scope asset is an expandable card. The header shows the asset name, an Active or Inactive badge, the asset types, and its criticality. Expand a card to see:

Section Description Overview Description, types, criticality, and state of the asset. Scope The registered targets — domains, URLs, IP ranges, API endpoints, app identifiers, and any testing notes. Attachments Supporting files such as API specs or scope documents. Test credentials Request a test account for this asset (see below).

docs.title: Scope definition
docs.text:
Field Description In scope What you may test — endpoints, environments, and vulnerability classes that qualify. Out of scope What is explicitly excluded. Reports on these items do not qualify for a reward.

Testing out-of-scope targets is a violation of platform guidelines.

docs.title: Program overview
docs.text: Organisation, number of in-scope assets, program type, Description, Rules of engagement, and the Safe harbor policy (when the program publishes one).

docs.title: Test credentials
docs.text:
Some assets offer test accounts. Each asset card has a Test credentials panel — "Request a test account for this asset. An admin reviews every request."

flowchart LR
    A[Request credentials] --> B([Pending review])
    B -->|approved| C([Approved — waiting for credentials])
    B -->|rejected| X([Rejected])
    C --> D([Credentials assigned])
    D --> E[Reveal credentials and test]
    E --> F[Release when finished]
  1. Click Request credentials on the asset.
  2. In the dialog, enter a Reason explaining what you plan to test (for example, "Testing authorization between tenant roles on the billing module."). A character counter shows the minimum and maximum length.
  3. Click Submit request. The panel shows the request status, with a View request link.
  4. When a credential set is assigned, the panel shows Credentials assigned with a Reveal credentials button and a Manage link.
  5. Revealed credentials hide automatically after a short time, and when you switch away from the tab. Reveal them again when you need them.

Credential requests open only while the program is Active. If an asset does not offer test accounts, the panel says so. Manage all your assignments and requests under My Credentials.

docs.title: Rules of engagement and testing guidelines
docs.text: Guideline Requirement Researcher identification Use any identification header or account the program asks for, so the client can identify your traffic. Rate limiting Keep scanning speeds within the limits in the rules of engagement. Data preservation Never modify, delete, or exfiltrate customer or organisational data. Stop and report once an exploit is confirmed. No disruptive testing No denial of service, credential brute-forcing, or social engineering unless the program explicitly allows it. Credentials Use only accounts assigned to you. Never share them, and release them when you finish.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem Cause / Solution No Request credentials button The program is not Active, the asset doesn't offer test accounts, or you already have an open request for it. Credentials cannot be viewed The program is paused, your access ended, or you no longer have access to the program. Check My Credentials. Unsure if a subdomain is in scope Wildcard entries (e.g. *.acme.test) include subdomains; a flat list includes only the exact domains. When in doubt, ask in Chat (private programs) before testing.

← Previous: Program Details Overview | Next: Rewards →

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: The Updates tab is the official communication board for the program. It is managed by the SecurityBoat triage staff and client administrators to keep researchers updated on critical program modifications.

docs.title: What is Posted in Updates?
docs.text:
Whenever an important change is made to the program, an update is posted. Common updates include:

Update Type Description Scope Expansions Notice of newly added assets or IP ranges. Scope Reductions Removal of assets that are undergoing maintenance or are no longer eligible for testing. Reward Boosts Temporary or permanent increases in reward values (e.g., "Double payouts on API vulnerabilities this week!"). Policy Adjustments Updates to safe harbor terms, report formatting requirements, or forbidden testing techniques.

docs.title: Reading Updates
docs.text:
Each update card displays:

Card Element Description Title The headline of the announcement. Author The SecurityBoat CSM or client manager who posted the update. Date Timestamp of publication. Content Rich text detailing the update.

Tip

Always check the Updates tab first before starting a testing session. This ensures you do not waste time testing retired assets or miss out on high-reward targets.

← Previous: Collaborators | Next: Chat →

docs.title: Engagements Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to the Pentest Engagements module. This guide details how Penetration Testing as a Service (PTaaS) engagements operate on the Tri-Netra platform and explains the structured workflows researchers follow during a penetration test.

Unlike continuous Bug Bounty programs, a PTaaS Engagement is a scheduled, team-based security assessment with a defined target scope, specific testing timeline, and structured methodology.

docs.title: The Engagement Lifecycle
docs.text:
Engagements progress through a series of states. Knowing where an engagement stands helps you align your testing and reporting activities:

graph LR
    Scheduled[Scheduled] --> Live[Live]
    Live --> Drafting[Report Drafting]
    Drafting --> Review[Report Review]
    Review --> Delivered[Delivered]
    Delivered --> Remediation[Remediation]
    Remediation --> Closed[Closed]

docs.title: Explanation of Lifecycle States
docs.text: State What It Means for You Scheduled The engagement dates are locked. You can review the scope and brief, but testing has not started yet. Live Testing is actively underway. Perform security tests, collaborate in Chat, check off items on the Coverage checklist, and submit findings in real time. Report Drafting The testing window has closed. The Lead Researcher writes the report and submits it for review (only possible in this state). Report Review The client signs the report off, then SecurityBoat completes the final review and marks it Final. Delivered The final report has been issued to the client. Remediation The client is patching vulnerabilities. You may be requested to perform targeted retests on fixed assets. Closed The engagement is complete. Details are preserved as read-only.

docs.title: Researcher Roles on Engagements
docs.text:
Your permissions and responsibilities depend on your assigned role:

  • Lead Researcher: Coordinates the pentest team, reviews finding submissions, monitors testing coverage, leads the report compilation, and communicates directly with SecurityBoat TPMs and CSMs.
  • Researcher: Performs security testing, documents coverage checkmarks, chats with the team, and submits findings.

docs.title: Navigating the Engagements List
docs.text:
To browse your assigned engagements, click Pentest Engagements in the main sidebar.

The listing page includes:

  1. Summary tiles: Total engagements, Live, and Completed (Delivered plus Closed).
  2. Filter pills (each with a count):
    • All: Every engagement you are assigned to.
    • Live: Engagements where active testing is underway.
    • Scheduled: Dates confirmed, testing not started yet.
    • Delivered: Report issued, including engagements in Remediation.
    • Closed: Finished engagements.
    • Requested and Archived: rarely used by researchers. Archived engagements have a read-only chat.
  3. Search & Table: Search by project ID or title… The table lists the engagement (title, Project ID, testing type), Client, State, TPM, Findings, and Scheduled dates.

Note

Click on any row in the table to open the Engagement Detail view.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Engagement Access
docs.text:
Issue Cause / Solution An engagement is missing from my list You must be on the engagement team — through an accepted application on Opportunities or an invitation on Invites. If you were removed from the team, the engagement is no longer listed, but findings you submitted stay visible under Findings. No Pentest Engagements in the sidebar PTaaS is not enabled for your account. Contact SecurityBoat. Testing target does not respond If target servers are down or blocking your IP, report it immediately in the engagement Chat tab to alert the TPM and Client. Cannot submit a finding Ensure the engagement state is Live. The Submit finding button only appears while the engagement accepts findings.

← Previous: Invites | Next: Engagement Detail: Brief →

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text: The Analytics tab provides visual representations and charts summarizing the vulnerability metrics for the engagement. It is a shared dashboard visible to the testing team and the client organization.

docs.title: Visual Dashboards
docs.text: The analytics page displays three primary metrics:

docs.title: 1. Severity Distribution
docs.text: A chart illustrating the breakdown of findings by severity rating (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational). This helps the client prioritize their development resources during the remediation phase.

docs.title: 2. Status Breakdown
docs.text: A chart showing the count of findings by lifecycle status (Draft, New, Verified, resolved, duplicate, etc.). This visualizes the progress of the triage and patching workflow.

docs.title: 3. Finding Trends
docs.text:
A timeline graph tracking the cumulative number of vulnerabilities discovered over the course of the testing window.

← Previous: Findings | Next: Reports →

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: The Assets tab houses the detailed technical information for each target item linked to the engagement. This page is essential for Grey-Box and White-Box testing, as it contains target details, IP ranges, mobile app binaries, API schemas, and active testing credentials.

docs.title: Assets Grid
docs.text:
The assets page presents a card grid or table listing each target asset:

Asset Field Description Asset Name A recognizable label (e.g., Staging Authentication API). Type Category of the asset (Web Application, API, Mobile, Network, Cloud, Source Code, AI/LLM Model). Target/URL The IP address, URL, or endpoint path. Asset Description Detailed context or testing goals specific to the asset.

docs.title: Testing Credentials & Accounts
docs.text:
For authenticated testing (Grey-Box/White-Box), the client provides credentials. These are secure login records attached directly to individual assets.

Each credential block includes:

Credential Field Description Role/Type The user role associated with the credentials (e.g., Standard User, Tenant Admin, Read-Only Viewer). Username / ID The email or username to authenticate with. Password / Key The password, API token, or SSH key. Testing Notes Guidance on how to authenticate, where to find MFA bypass codes, or specific paths to test with these credentials.

docs.title: Secure Asset Handling Guidelines
docs.text:
Credential Confidentiality

Credentials provided for testing are strictly confidential. Do not share them outside the engagement team or use them after the testing window closes.

Handling Principle Standard Protocol Credential Verification Verify all login credentials on the first day of the Live phase. If credentials are locked, expired, or have insufficient permissions, report it immediately in the engagement Chat tab. MFA Bypass If Multi-Factor Authentication is enabled on a target, clients may provide a static bypass code or a shared TOTP secret (listed in the credentials card) to enable automated or manual testing.

← Previous: Brief | Next: Team →

docs.title: Brief
docs.text: The Brief tab is the default landing view when you open a pentest engagement. It provides a complete overview of the engagement's configuration, rules of engagement, testing schedule, and assigned team.

docs.title: Page Layout Diagram
docs.text:
The Brief tab is organized into a two-column layout as illustrated below:

graph TD
    Brief[Brief Tab Layout] --> Left[Left Column: Configuration & Scope]
    Brief --> Right[Right Column: Sidebar Metrics]
    Left --> MetricChips[Metric Chips: Type, Approach, Environment, Source-code]
    Left --> Desc[Description]
    Left --> RoE[Rules of Engagement: In-scope vs Out-of-scope]
    Right --> Schedule[Schedule: Window progress, Dates, Effort]
    Right --> Team[Team: Lead, Researchers]
    Right --> History[State History: Timeline]

docs.title: 1. Configuration Metric Chips
docs.text:
Four key parameters define the testing environment:

Chip Parameter Supported Target Categories / Options Engagement Types Web Application, API, Mobile, Network, Cloud, IoT, Source Code. Testing Approach Black box (no info), Grey box (credentials/details provided), or White box (full access). Environment Production, Staging, QA, Development. Source-Code Access Indicates if repositories have been shared (Granted / Not Granted).

docs.title: 2. Project Description
docs.text: Contains high-level objectives, business context, or specific focus areas requested by the client.

docs.title: 3. Rules of Engagement
docs.text:
Defines target constraints:

Scope Category Description In-Scope Targets Domains, IPs, and code repos authorized for probing. Out-of-Scope Targets Systems, endpoints, or third-party integrations strictly excluded from testing.

docs.title: 1. Schedule & Effort
docs.text: Schedule Field Description Window Progress A visual bar showing the percentage of the testing timeline that has elapsed. Scheduled Dates Planned start and end dates. Actual Dates Timestamps of when the testing phase actually started and finished. Testing Effort (hrs) Total allocated hours budgeted for the assessment.

docs.title: 2. Testing Team Card
docs.text: Lists the security team members assigned to this engagement, categorized by role (Lead Researcher, Researcher) with their names and contact emails.

docs.title: 3. State History Card
docs.text:
A vertical timeline tracking every lifecycle transition of the engagement, showing when it moved from one state to another (e.g., Scheduled to Live).

← Previous: Engagements Overview | Next: Assets →

docs.title: Chat
docs.text: The Chat tab is a secure, real-time messaging workspace built into the engagement detail page. It enables researchers to communicate directly with other testing team members, SecurityBoat project managers, and the client organization.

docs.title: Channels & Scope
docs.text:
The chat tab is structured as a multi-party group channel containing:

Roster Party Platform Role Testing Team Assigned Researchers and the Lead Researcher. SecurityBoat Management The assigned Technical Project Manager (TPM) and Customer Success Manager (CSM). Client Organization Client Administrators and Client TPMs (Client Viewers can read).

docs.title: Message audiences
docs.text:
• Your messages are posted to Everyone — the testing team, SecurityBoat staff, and the client team.
  • SecurityBoat may post messages to the Researchers audience, which only the testing team and SecurityBoat can read.
  • The client and SecurityBoat also have audiences that researchers do not see, so you may not see every message in the thread.

docs.title: Mentions
docs.text: Type @ to mention a participant who can read the message. They receive a notification.

docs.title: When to Use Chat
docs.text:
The chat tab is the primary channel for operational communication during testing:

Scenario Objective Credential Blockers Ask the client to reset password locks or update expired accounts. IP Whitelisting Request that client system administrators whitelist testing IP addresses if firewall blocks occur. Scope Inquiries Ask for clarification on wildcard subdomains or testing endpoints. PoC Discussion Discuss reproduction steps or technical impacts with client developers.

docs.title: Chat Best Practices
docs.text:
Please observe the following guidelines when using the chat:

Guideline Policy / Protocol No Finding Writeups Do not write complete vulnerability reports or paste exploit scripts in the chat. Use the Submit Finding drawer for reports. Keep it Centralized Avoid using external communication channels. Centralizing chat ensures all updates are recorded. Professionalism Maintain a constructive, professional tone at all times.

← Previous: Edit Narrative | Back to: Engagements Overview

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
The Coverage tab is where the testing team tracks and documents the progress of the security assessment. It provides a structured methodology checklist based on the type of assets under review.

Completing the coverage checklist is a critical requirement of the penetration test. It demonstrates to the client that a thorough, systematic assessment was conducted, rather than just running automated scanners.

docs.title: Logging Coverage Workflow
docs.text:
The flowchart below illustrates the process for completing and logging a methodology checklist item:

graph TD
    Test[Perform Test Check] --> Decision{Is Feature Present?}
    Decision -->|Yes| Tested[Mark Status: Tested + Add Test Notes]
    Decision -->|No| NA[Mark Status: Not Applicable + Add Justification]
    Tested --> Progress[Completion Progress Bar Updates]
    NA --> Progress

docs.title: Methodology Checklists
docs.text:
The checklists are automatically populated based on the engagement type. Common frameworks include:

Framework Target Category OWASP Top 10 Web Applications OWASP API Security Top 10 APIs & Web Services OWASP MASVS Mobile Applications (iOS / Android) NIST SP 800-115 Network Infrastructure & Servers

docs.title: Recording Testing Coverage
docs.text:
During the Live phase, as you complete specific testing checks, you must document your progress:

  1. Checkoff: Mark the checkbox next to the completed testing item (e.g., Verify password policy enforcement).
  2. Add Testing Context: Configure the following fields in the checklist item drawer:
Context Field Requirement Status Mark as Tested (fully verified), Not Applicable (the feature is not present on the target), or In Progress. Assigned Tester Select your name from the assigned testers dropdown list. Notes Add a brief note detailing paths or parameters tested, tools used, or manual results (especially if marking as "Not Applicable").

docs.title: Collaborative Progress Tracking
docs.text:
The coverage tab features a visual progress bar indicating the overall completion percentage of the checklist.

  • Real-time Updates: Both the client organization and the SecurityBoat TPM can monitor the progress bar.
  • Lead Researcher Review: The Lead Researcher reviews the notes and ensures all checklist items are fully resolved before transitioning the engagement to the Report Drafting phase.

← Previous: Team | Next: Findings →

docs.title: Edit Narrative
docs.text: The Edit Narrative workspace allows authorized authors to draft and refine the key qualitative sections of the engagement report.

docs.title: Editor Access & Role Delegation
docs.text:
Edit capability is strictly delegated to ensure quality control and clear segregation of duties:

Role Type Edit Capability Role Description & Control Lead Researcher Authorized The primary author responsible for writing the technical findings, summary of recommendations, and scope details. Technical Project Manager Authorized Can edit the narrative during drafting or review to refine language, format structure, or fix description errors. Customer Success Manager Authorized Can edit sections to align executive summaries and business contexts with customer expectations. Platform Administrator Authorized Holds complete editing permissions and serves as the final arbiter for formatting and scope details. Client / Customer None Cannot edit. The client previews the report, then approves it or requests changes once it is submitted for review. Standard Researcher None Excluded from editing and report preview access. Standard testing team members focus strictly on findings and coverage logs.

docs.title: Key Narrative Components
docs.text: Authorized authors use a rich-text editor to configure five core sections:

docs.title: 1. Title Page Configuration
docs.text: • Report Title (required): The title printed on the report cover. The scheduled month and year are added automatically (for example "— Oct — 2026"), so enter the title without a date. You cannot save the narrative without a title — the save button shows "Enter a report title before saving" and the form shows "A report title is required."

docs.title: 2. Executive Summary
docs.text:
• Purpose: A brief, high-level summary of the assessment goals, timeline, and results.
  • Audience: Designed for executive stakeholders who need a quick summary of the security outcome.

docs.title: 3. Executive Analysis
docs.text:
• Purpose: Deep-dive analysis highlighting root causes, technical vulnerability trends, and residual risk.
  • Audience: Designed for security managers and directors to understand broader risk patterns.

docs.title: 4. Summary of Recommendations
docs.text:
• Purpose: A structured summary of the top remediation priorities.
  • Audience: Actionable guidance for the client engineering and operations teams.

docs.title: 5. Assessment Limitations
docs.text:
• Purpose: Documents any testing constraints (e.g. time limits, restricted testing windows, or system downtime).
  • Audience: Provides context for the final coverage results.

docs.title: Prefill Templates
docs.text:
To accelerate report drafting, the platform automatically generates prefill templates when editing begins. These templates pull metadata from the engagement context to dynamically populate:

  • The client organization name.
  • The target asset title.
  • The total number of researchers assigned.
  • The scheduled start and end dates.

docs.title: Saving vs. Submitting
docs.text:
• Saving Progress: Clicking Save Progress writes the latest narrative updates. It does not change the report status. Editing and saving are possible only while the engagement is Live or in Report drafting.
  • Submitting for Review: Once drafting is finished, the Lead Researcher clicks Submit for review. This works only when the engagement is in Report drafting and methodology coverage is 100%. The report then goes to the client for sign-off, followed by SecurityBoat's final review. See Reports.

← Previous: Reports | Next: Chat →

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: The Findings tab shows the security issues found during the engagement. It is your workspace for submitting new findings and tracking existing ones.

docs.title: Findings list
docs.text:
Column Description Finding ID Reference ID (e.g. PT-ACME-01). Title Vulnerability summary. Severity Derived from the CVSS v4.0 score. State Draft, Triaging, Verified, Fix in progress, Ready for retest, Accepted risk, or Resolved. Asset The asset where the issue was found.

Use the severity and state filters to narrow the list (for example, state = Ready for retest to see what you need to re-test). Export CSV lets you choose the columns to download.

Click a row to open the finding's detail page to read comments, see triage feedback, or edit the finding.

docs.title: Submitting a finding
docs.text:
While the engagement is Live, click Submit finding at the top right of the tab. A drawer opens with the finding form.

The form covers title and classification (asset type, OWASP vulnerability type, VRT category, CWE, optional CVE and MITRE ATT&CK), the 11 CVSS v4.0 metrics, the writeup (Background, Description, Steps to reproduce, Impact, Remediation), CIA impact, OWASP likelihood and impact, references, and the endpoint and HTTP evidence.

  1. Click Create finding. The finding is saved as a Draft.
  2. Open it and use State actions → Submit DRAFT for triage → Confirm transition.

See Findings → Submitting a finding for every field and its rules.

docs.title: Editing a finding
docs.text:
Pentest findings stay editable after submission. Open the finding and click Edit finding.

  • A Researcher can edit findings they submitted. A Lead Researcher can edit any finding on the engagement.
  • Editing is possible until the finding is Resolved.
  • Severity and CVSS are locked once the finding is Verified.

docs.title: Lifecycle and retesting
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    DR([Draft]) -->|submit| TR([Triaging])
    TR -->|lead or TPM verifies| V([Verified])
    V -->|client| F([Fix in progress])
    F -->|client| R([Ready for retest])
    R -->|Confirm fix verified| D([Resolved])
    R -->|Retest failed| F
  • Triage: the Lead Researcher or TPM uses Verify finding (disclose to client), or declines it, marks it as a duplicate, or marks it out of scope with a reason. They can also Request more information.
  • Retest: when the client moves a finding to Ready for retest, the original researcher or the Lead Researcher re-runs the reproduction steps:
    • Fixed → Confirm fix verified → Resolved.
    • Still vulnerable → Retest failed — send back to fix with a comment (at least 20 characters) → Fix in progress.
  • The Retest SLA card on the finding shows the time left while a retest is pending.

← Previous: Coverage | Next: Analytics →

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
The Reports tab is the workspace for the engagement report. It is visible to the Lead Researcher, the client, and SecurityBoat staff.

Role restriction

Standard Researchers do not see this tab. The Lead Researcher writes and submits the report.

docs.title: Report lifecycle
docs.text:
The report is signed off in two stages: first by the client, then by SecurityBoat.

flowchart LR
    D([Draft]) -->|Lead: Submit for review| IR([In review])
    IR -->|client: Approve report| CA([Client Approved])
    IR -->|client: Request changes| RJ([Rejected])
    RJ -->|Lead revises and resubmits| IR
    CA -->|SecurityBoat: Mark Final| F([✓ Final])
    CA -->|SecurityBoat sends back| RJ
    F -->|after retest| PR([✓ Post-Retest Final])
Status What it means Draft The Lead Researcher is writing the narrative. In review Submitted. The client (Client Admin or Client TPM) reviews it. Rejected Changes were requested. Revise and resubmit. Client Approved The client approved it; SecurityBoat is doing the final review. ✓ Final Released to the client for download. ✓ Post-Retest Final Re-issued after findings were retested.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Action Who When Preview the report Lead Researcher, client, SecurityBoat Any status Edit narrative and Save progress Lead Researcher, SecurityBoat While the engagement is Live or in Report drafting Submit for review Lead Researcher, SecurityBoat Report is Draft or Rejected, the engagement is in Report drafting, and methodology coverage is 100% Approve report / Request changes Client Admin, Client TPM Report is In review Mark Final SecurityBoat Report is Client Approved Re-issue (post-retest) SecurityBoat Report is Final Download PDF Client and SecurityBoat Clients from Final onward. The Lead Researcher previews but does not download.

docs.title: Submit-for-review checks
docs.text:
Submit for review is always shown on a Draft or Rejected report, but it only works when:

  1. The engagement is in Report drafting. Otherwise you see: "A report can only be submitted while the engagement is in Report Drafting."
  2. Methodology coverage is 100%. The tab shows "✓ Methodology coverage 100% … Ready to submit for review." when every required item on the Coverage tab is marked; otherwise it asks you to mark every item first.

Outside Live and Report drafting, Edit narrative and Submit for review are shown blurred with a tooltip explaining why.

docs.title: Narrative sections
docs.text:
Section Renders in Guidelines Title Report cover Required. The scheduled month and year are added automatically (e.g. "— Oct — 2026"), so don't type them. Executive Summary Summary section What was tested, when, and the headline outcome. Executive Analysis Summary section Vulnerability trends, root causes, and risk themes. Assessment Limitations Constraints section Optional. Hidden if empty. Summary of Recommendations Priority recommendations The top remediation priorities for the client.

See Edit Narrative for the editor.

docs.title: Scope tables
docs.text:
The Lead Researcher also maintains the scope tables, which map assets to their environments. The environment can be Production, UAT, Staging, QA, or Development.

Asset type Columns Web Application URL, Environment API / Web Services Base URL, Environment Mobile Application App Name/Binary, Bundle ID, Platform, Environment Cloud Infrastructure Account / Subscription ID, Region, Environment Thick Client App Name, Version, Environment IoT / Embedded Device Name, Firmware Version, Environment Other Name, Notes

docs.title: Document control
docs.text:
Every action (submit, approve, request changes, mark final, re-issue) asks for a Description of Changes of at least 5 characters. The note is saved to the version history and printed in the report's document-control log.

If a report waits more than 3 days for client review, the client and TPM are reminded.

← Previous: Analytics | Next: Edit Narrative →

docs.title: Team
docs.text: The Team tab lists the full security team roster assigned to the engagement, outlining who is participating from both the SecurityBoat side and the client organization.

docs.title: Communication & Collaboration Hierarchy
docs.text:
The hierarchy diagram below illustrates how communication flows during an engagement:

graph TD
    Client[Client Admin / Client TPM] <--> PM[SecurityBoat TPM / CSM]
    PM <--> Lead[Lead Researcher]
    Lead <--> Researchers[Testing Researchers]

docs.title: Roster Classification
docs.text: The team page classifies members by their role on the project:

docs.title: 1. SecurityBoat Testing Team
docs.text: Role Responsibilities Lead Researcher The primary technical contact. Coordinates the testing team, reviews findings, ensures coverage checklist completion, and drafts the executive report. Researchers Security engineers responsible for identifying vulnerabilities, documenting coverage, and submitting findings.

docs.title: 2. SecurityBoat Project Management
docs.text: Role Responsibilities TPM (Technical Project Manager) Coordinates the project timeline, manages scheduling, and triages submitted findings. Serves as the escalation point for technical blockers. CSM (Customer Success Manager) Ensures overall client satisfaction and handles commercial or administrative questions.

docs.title: 3. Client Team
docs.text: Role Responsibilities Client Admin / Client TPM The client representatives who requested the pentest. They receive notifications, discuss findings in chat, and coordinate remediation.

docs.title: Communication Protocols
docs.text:
For Technical Questions

Use the engagement Chat tab to discuss target behavior, credential errors, or testing blockages. This keeps the communications centralized and visible to both the testing team and the client.

  • For Severity Queries: If you have a question about how a finding is classified or need clarification on a duplicate triage state, message your assigned TPM or Lead Researcher directly.
